The zero-resistance state and the flux quantization remain the defining experimental signatures. Both follow from the existence of a macroscopic coherent phase.

title: The Precision of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Quantum electrodynamics is the theory of electrons, positrons, and photons. It is the most precisely tested theory in physics. The magnetic moment of the electron is predicted and measured to more than ten significant figures. The agreement holds.

The Dirac equation gives the electron a g-factor of exactly 2. Quantum corrections change it. The leading correction, calculated by Schwinger in 1948, is \( a = (g-2)/2 = \alpha/(2\pi) \), where \( \alpha \) is the fine-structure constant. Higher-order terms in powers of \( \alpha \) have been calculated. The experimental value of the anomaly is \( a_e = 0.00115965218059(13) \). The theoretical value, limited by the precision of \( \alpha \) itself, matches within the uncertainties.

The Lamb shift is the splitting between the \( 2s_{1/2} \) and \( 2p_{1/2} \) levels of hydrogen. In the Dirac theory they are degenerate. The measured interval is about 1057 MHz. The dominant contribution comes from the electron’s interaction with the fluctuating electromagnetic field. A smaller contribution, about −27 MHz, comes from vacuum polarization, the Uehling effect. The full calculation, including higher orders, matches the measurement.

The fine-structure constant is not constant. It runs with the energy scale. Vacuum polarization screens the charge at long distances. At shorter distances the effective charge is larger. The running is logarithmic. At the mass of the Z boson, \( 1/\alpha \) is about 128.9 rather than 137.0. The running is measured in scattering experiments and is consistent with the calculation.

Renormalization is the procedure that makes these predictions finite. Loop diagrams produce divergent integrals. The divergences are absorbed into the definitions of the measured mass and charge. Once those quantities are fixed by experiment, the remaining predictions are finite and unambiguous. The procedure is not an arbitrary subtraction. It is required by the structure of the theory and is constrained by gauge invariance. The Ward identity ensures that the renormalization of the vertex and of the electron field are related, so that the charge remains universal.

The precision is possible because the expansion parameter \( \alpha \) is small. Each additional loop is suppressed by another factor of \( \alpha/\pi \). The same methods applied to the strong force do not converge in the same way at low energy. QED is both a working computational tool and a demonstration that a quantum field theory can be defined, renormalized, and tested to extraordinary accuracy. Its success fixes the standard against which other theories are judged.

title: Maxwell’s Equations
paras: James Clerk Maxwell unified electricity and magnetism in 1865. He did this without the aid of a committee, which may explain why it worked. The four equations that bear his name describe all classical electromagnetic phenomena. They also predict that light is an electromagnetic wave, a result that was considered rather sporting of them.

The first equation is Gauss’s law for electricity. The flux of the electric field through any closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by the permittivity of free space. In differential form it states that the divergence of the electric field is proportional to the charge density. Charge is the source of the electric field. There are no magnetic monopoles. The corresponding equation for the magnetic field states that the flux of the magnetic field through any closed surface is zero. The divergence of the magnetic field is zero. Magnetic field lines form closed loops.

Faraday’s law states that a changing magnetic flux through a circuit induces an electromotive force. In differential form the curl of the electric field equals the negative of the rate of change of the magnetic field. A changing magnetic field produces an electric field. The direction is given by Lenz’s law: the induced field opposes the change that produces it.

Ampère’s law, as corrected by Maxwell, states that the curl of the magnetic field is proportional to the total current density plus the displacement current. The displacement current is the term Maxwell added: the rate of change of the electric field. A changing electric field produces a magnetic field, just as a changing magnetic field produces an electric field. The two fields can sustain each other.

In free space, with no charges or currents, the equations combine to give wave equations for both fields. The waves travel at the speed \( c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0} \). That speed matches the measured speed of light. Light is an electromagnetic wave. The same equations describe radio waves, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays. They differ only in frequency.

The equations are linear. Solutions can be superposed. They are also Lorentz invariant. The same equations hold in every inertial frame when the fields are transformed correctly. That invariance was one of the clues that led to special relativity. The classical theory is complete within its domain. It fails at the quantum level, where the field is quantized and the photon appears, and it fails at the Planck scale, where gravity cannot be ignored. Within the domain of classical electromagnetism the equations remain exact.

title: Collective Electrodynamics
paras: Carver Mead has argued that the electromagnetic field can be understood as a consequence of the quantum phase of charged particles rather than as an independent entity. In this view the vector potential is the fundamental object. It sets the phase standard for the electrons. The electric and magnetic fields are derived quantities.

The starting point is the phase of the electron wave function. A charged particle moving in a potential acquires a phase proportional to the line integral of the vector potential. When many electrons share a common phase, as they do in a superconductor, the collective phase is a macroscopic observable. The supercurrent is proportional to the gradient of that phase. The magnetic field is related to the curl of the potential, and the quantization of flux follows from the requirement that the phase be single-valued around a closed loop.

From the collective behavior one can recover Maxwell’s equations. The electric field appears as the force that changes the momentum, and the magnetic field appears as the quantity whose flux is quantized. The energy and momentum stored in the fields can be expressed in terms of the potentials and the charges. The classical fields are the large-scale description of the underlying phase relationships.

The approach does not replace quantum electrodynamics. It offers a different route to the same classical limit, beginning from the quantum mechanics of the charges rather than from the fields. It makes the Aharonov–Bohm effect and the Josephson effect natural rather than surprising, because both are direct statements about phase. It also clarifies why the potentials, which are gauge-dependent, can still have physical consequences: the gauge-invariant phase differences are what the charges measure.

The account is consistent with experiment. It does not alter any tested prediction of classical electromagnetism or of QED. It changes the order of explanation. The fields are what the charges do, collectively, when their phases are taken into account. Whether this order is more fundamental is a question of interpretation. The mathematics and the measurements remain the same.

title: Feynman’s Account of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Richard Feynman presented quantum electrodynamics in a form that begins with amplitudes rather than with fields. Every photon carries a complex amplitude, which can be drawn as an arrow. The arrow has a length and a direction. The probability that an event occurs is the square of the length of the final arrow. When an event can happen in more than one way, the arrows for the different ways are added before the square is taken. Interference is the result of that addition. Nature, it seems, prefers to do the arithmetic first and the squaring later, which is the opposite of the order most of us learned in school and have been regretting ever since.

Light is partially reflected from a surface of glass. The probability depends on the thickness of the glass. The calculation sums the amplitudes for reflection from the front surface and from the back surface. The relative phase depends on the extra distance traveled. The same rule accounts for the reflection from a mirror, the focusing of a lens, and the diffraction by a grating. In each case every possible path contributes an amplitude. Paths near the classical path have nearly the same phase and add constructively. Paths far from the classical path cancel.

An electron also carries an amplitude for going from one point to another. The amplitude depends on the proper time along the path. An electron can emit or absorb a photon. Those three processes—the photon going from place to place, the electron going from place to place, and the electron emitting or absorbing a photon—are the only ingredients. Every electromagnetic process is a combination of them. The combinations are drawn as diagrams. Each diagram corresponds to a term in the calculation. The terms are added, and the square of the sum is the probability.

The theory is approximate. Higher-order diagrams contain loops and produce large intermediate numbers. Those numbers are absorbed into the measured mass and charge of the electron. Once that is done, the remaining predictions are finite. The magnetic moment of the electron, the Lamb shift, and the scattering of light by light are calculated and measured to high precision. The agreement is the strongest quantitative success in physics.

The account does not eliminate the mathematics. It shows what the mathematics is doing. Amplitudes are added for every way an event can happen. The classical path is the path that survives the addition. The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field. The same rules govern the emission of light by an atom, the reflection of light by a mirror, and the forces between charges. The strangeness is not removed. It is located in the rule that the arrows must be added before they are squared.

title: The Technical Structure of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Feynman’s formulation of quantum electrodynamics supplies a set of rules for calculating any electromagnetic process. The amplitude for a particle to go from one point to another is given by a propagator. For the electron the propagator is the Green function of the Dirac equation. For the photon it is the Green function of the wave equation. Both are known in closed form.

An interaction occurs when an electron emits or absorbs a photon. The vertex contributes a factor proportional to the charge and to the Dirac matrix \(\gamma^\mu\). Momentum is conserved at every vertex. The full amplitude for a process is the sum of the amplitudes for every diagram that connects the initial state to the final state. Each internal line is a propagator. Each closed loop is integrated over the momentum that circulates in it.

The path-integral version of the same theory states that the amplitude is the sum over all field histories of \(e^{iS/\hbar}\), where \(S\) is the classical action. The Feynman rules are the perturbative expansion of that sum. The two formulations are equivalent. The diagrams are a bookkeeping device for the expansion. They are not pictures of trajectories.

Ultraviolet divergences appear in the loop integrals. They are handled by renormalization. The bare mass and charge in the Lagrangian are not the measured mass and charge. The difference absorbs the divergent parts. After renormalization every physical prediction is finite. Infrared divergences appear when massless photons are emitted with vanishing energy. They cancel in any observable that sums over all soft photons that cannot be resolved. The cancellation is required by the structure of the theory.

The same rules give the anomalous magnetic moment, the Lamb shift, the running of the charge, and the cross sections for scattering and pair production. Each additional loop is suppressed by a power of the fine-structure constant. The expansion is therefore practical. The theory remains the prototype of a renormalizable quantum field theory. Its rules are specific to electrons and photons. The same diagrammatic method, with different vertices and propagators, is used for the other forces.

title: The Horizon and Flatness Problems
paras: The hot Big Bang accounts for the expansion, the microwave background, and the abundances of the light elements. It leaves two puzzles. The first is the horizon problem. The cosmic microwave background is uniform to one part in a hundred thousand in every direction. Regions that are now on opposite sides of the sky were never in causal contact in the standard expanding model. They had no time to exchange heat or information. Yet they have the same temperature. The second is the flatness problem. The density of the universe is close to the critical density that separates expansion forever from eventual recollapse. The critical density is unstable. A small departure early on grows rapidly. To be as close as it is today, the density at one second after the Big Bang had to match the critical value to one part in 10^15 or better. No mechanism in the standard model explains either fact.

Inflation supplies a mechanism. A brief period of accelerated expansion, driven by a scalar field in a false vacuum, stretches a small, causally connected region to a size larger than the present observable universe. The region is smoothed. Temperature differences are erased. The same expansion drives the density toward the critical value, so that the universe appears flat. The quantum fluctuations of the field are stretched to cosmic scales and become the seeds of later structure. The spectrum of those fluctuations is nearly scale-invariant. It matches the pattern measured in the microwave background and in the large-scale distribution of galaxies.

The idea was proposed in the early 1980s. It is not yet derived from a confirmed particle-physics model. The field that drove it has not been identified. The duration and the energy scale remain free parameters within broad limits. What the observations require is some process that produced a large, nearly uniform, nearly flat region with small density perturbations of the observed amplitude. Inflation is the leading candidate. Other proposals exist. None has yet replaced it. The problems it solves were already visible in the 1970s. The microwave data that confirmed the uniformity and the flatness arrived later. The sequence is the reverse of the usual one: the solution was offered before the precision measurements that made the problems sharp.

title: Natural Selection Without a Designer
paras: The appearance of design in living things is real. The eye focuses. The wing generates lift. The enzyme catalyzes a reaction at a rate that would otherwise take longer than the age of the universe. For centuries the inference was that such arrangements required a designer. The inference is unnecessary.

Natural selection is a process that produces cumulative adaptation without foresight. Variation exists. Some variants leave more offspring than others. The difference is heritable. Over generations the population changes. The change is not random. It is directed by the differential success of the variants in the environment they actually inhabit. The direction is local and retrospective. It does not aim at a distant goal. It does not require that any organism understand the process.

The cumulative character is essential. A single mutation rarely produces a complex organ. A sequence of mutations, each preserved because it conferred a small advantage in its own generation, can. The intermediates need not be useful for the final function. They need only be useful for something at the time they appear. The history is recoverable in the fossil record, in comparative anatomy, and in the sequences of genes. The same gene families appear in organisms that use them for different purposes. The pattern is the pattern of descent with modification, not the pattern of separate creation.

The process has no designer and no plan. It also has no guarantee of progress in any global sense. Lineages go extinct. Complexity can decrease. What it does guarantee is that, given variation, heritability, and differential reproduction, adaptation will accumulate where the conditions allow. The conditions have allowed it for more than three billion years. The result is the diversity of life. The mechanism is ordinary. The outcome is not.

title: Quantum Effects in Genetics
paras: Most genetic processes are classical. Base pairing, replication, transcription, and translation are described by ordinary chemistry. A few steps show quantum signatures that affect the outcome.

Proton tunneling contributes to some mutation rates. In DNA the hydrogen bonds that hold base pairs together can shift by tunneling. The tautomeric forms that result can mispair during replication. The rate is low. It is not zero. The contribution is measurable in some systems by comparing rates in ordinary water and in heavy water. The difference is consistent with a tunneling component. The bulk of mutations still arise from other causes: copying errors, chemical damage, and radiation. Tunneling is one channel among several.

Electron transfer in some repair enzymes and in photosynthetic reaction centers proceeds by tunneling. The distance dependence and the temperature dependence match quantum calculations. The proteins position the donors and acceptors so that the tunneling rate is useful. The positioning is the product of selection. The tunneling itself is a physical fact that selection has used.

No evidence currently supports the claim that genetic information is stored or processed in a macroscopic quantum superposition inside the cell. Decoherence times at biological temperatures and in the wet environment of the nucleus are extremely short. The successful descriptions of heredity, development, and evolution remain classical. The quantum contributions that have been demonstrated are local, specific, and already incorporated into the ordinary chemical account. They do not require a separate quantum genetics. They show that the chemistry of life includes the quantum mechanics of its atoms.

title: The Omega Point
paras: Frank Tipler has proposed that the universe will end in a final singularity, the Omega Point, in which infinite information processing becomes possible. In that state, he argues, every past event can be reconstructed and every possible mind can be emulated. The proposal is a cosmological conjecture joined to a claim about computation.

The conjecture requires that the universe recollapse and that the collapse be sufficiently chaotic for the available energy to be used for computation without limit. Current observations indicate that the expansion is accelerating. A recollapse is not expected. Even if the expansion later reversed, the conditions required for unbounded computation are not known to be satisfied. The second law still applies. The entropy of the universe increases. The energy available for computation is finite in any region that remains finite.

The further claim is that a sufficiently powerful computation could resurrect every person who has ever lived by simulating them. The claim assumes that a simulation of a person is the person. That assumption is contested. It also assumes that the required information about each person survives or can be reconstructed. Most information about individual lives is not preserved. The proposal does not supply a mechanism that recovers it.

The Omega Point is therefore a speculative extrapolation. It is not a prediction of established cosmology. It is not ruled out by logic alone. It is not supported by the evidence that currently exists. The accelerating expansion, the second law, and the absence of a known information-recovery process are the obstacles. They are substantial.

title: The End of Time
paras: Julian Barbour has argued that time is not fundamental. What exists, on this view, are configurations of the universe. Each configuration is a possible arrangement of all particles and fields. The configurations are related by records. A record is a structure within one configuration that is correlated with another configuration. The correlation is what we call a memory or a history. There is no external time in which the configurations occur. There is only the landscape of configurations and the records that link some of them.

The proposal is motivated by the problem of time in quantum gravity. The Wheeler–DeWitt equation, which is the quantum constraint for a closed universe, contains no time variable. Solutions are static. Barbour interprets the static character as evidence that time is absent at the fundamental level. Change is real only as a relation between configurations. The experienced flow of time is the experience of records being read.

The account does not deny the utility of time in ordinary physics. Clocks work. Predictions that use time succeed. The claim is that time is an emergent description, useful inside the universe and absent from the fundamental equation. The claim is not universally accepted. Other approaches to quantum gravity retain a notion of time or replace it with a different structure. The absence of a time variable in one equation does not by itself prove that time does not exist. It proves that that equation does not contain it.

The idea is a possible reading of the mathematics. It is not an established result. Experiments continue to use time. No observation has shown that time fails. The proposal remains an interpretation of the formalism of quantum cosmology, not a replacement for the time that clocks measure.

title: Adaptive Mutation and Quantum Coherence
paras: In 1999 Johnjoe McFadden and Jim Al-Khalili proposed a quantum model for adaptive mutation. Adaptive mutation is the reported phenomenon in which certain mutations appear more frequently when they confer an advantage than when they are neutral. The classical expectation is that mutation rates are independent of utility. The observations, first described in bacteria under starvation, have been disputed. Some are explained by ordinary growth and selection on pre-existing variants. Others remain unresolved.

The quantum proposal begins with proton tunneling in DNA base pairs. A proton can occupy either of two positions. The two positions correspond to different base-pairing possibilities. The model treats the proton as remaining in a coherent superposition of the two positions for a biologically relevant time. Interaction with an environment that contains a usable substrate is argued to accelerate decoherence and thereby increase the rate at which the mutant state is realized. The estimated decoherence time in the model is on the order of seconds. That is long enough, in principle, for the proposed effect.

The proposal has not been confirmed. Direct measurements of coherence in DNA under cellular conditions have not shown the required superposition. Decoherence calculations that include more of the molecular environment yield shorter times. The adaptive-mutation experiments themselves have alternative classical explanations in many cases. The idea remains a possible mechanism for a disputed phenomenon. It is not an established modification of evolutionary theory.

McFadden and Al-Khalili later surveyed a wider set of quantum effects in biology: tunneling in enzymes, coherent energy transfer in photosynthesis, the radical-pair mechanism for magnetoreception, and a proposed vibration-assisted tunneling in olfaction. Some of these effects are measured. Their functional importance varies. The adaptive-mutation model is the most specific claim that quantum coherence could bias the generation of heritable variation. That claim is still open. The broader observation that quantum mechanics is part of the chemistry of life is not.

title: Quantum Biology and Evolution
paras: Evolution is a classical process at the scale of populations. Mutation, selection, drift, and recombination are described by ordinary population genetics. The underlying chemistry of mutation and catalysis includes quantum steps. Those steps do not change the structure of the evolutionary account. They change the rates and the channels through which variation appears.

Proton and electron tunneling contribute to mutation. A proton that tunnels across a hydrogen bond in a base pair can produce a tautomeric form that mispairs. The contribution is small compared with copying errors and chemical damage. It is measurable in some systems by isotope effects. Electron tunneling occurs in the active sites of some repair enzymes. The proteins have evolved to position the reactants so that the tunneling rate is useful. The positioning is classical. The transfer step is quantum. Selection acts on the outcome, not on the mechanism.

Photosynthetic energy transfer and enzyme catalysis show coherent or tunneling contributions under physiological conditions. These processes affect the efficiency with which organisms capture energy and carry out metabolism. Efficiency is a selectable trait. Organisms that harness the quantum step more effectively leave more offspring, other things equal. The quantum step itself is not selected. The molecular architecture that makes the step available is selected. The distinction matters. Evolution does not need to “know” about quantum mechanics. It needs only to retain variants that work.

No established mechanism allows a cell to maintain a macroscopic superposition of genetic states and to collapse that superposition preferentially toward adaptive outcomes. The adaptive-mutation model remains a proposal. Decoherence in the cellular environment is rapid. The successful description of the origin and spread of adaptations continues to be the classical one: variation arises, most of it is neutral or deleterious, a fraction is advantageous, and selection increases the frequency of the advantageous fraction. Quantum mechanics is part of the physics that generates the variation and powers the metabolism. It is not a separate evolutionary force.

The practical consequence is modest and real. Calculations of mutation rates, of catalytic rates, and of energy-transfer efficiency are more accurate when the quantum channels are included. The evolutionary conclusions drawn from those rates do not change. The tree of life, the genetic code, and the history of adaptations remain the same. Quantum biology refines the chemistry. It does not rewrite the theory of evolution.

title: The Anthropic Principle
paras: The values of the fundamental constants permit the existence of carbon-based life. Small changes in several of them would prevent it. The strong force, if slightly stronger, would bind the diproton and alter the path of stellar nucleosynthesis. If slightly weaker, deuterium would be unbound and the same path would close. The electromagnetic force and the electron-to-proton mass ratio set the sizes of atoms and the stability of molecules. The cosmological constant, if much larger, would have prevented the formation of galaxies. These relations are observed. They are not explained by a deeper theory that derives the constants.

The weak anthropic principle states that the observed values are restricted by the requirement that observers exist to measure them. Observers can exist only in regions or in universes where the constants allow the formation of stable nuclei, long-lived stars, planets, and chemistry complex enough for life. The principle is a selection effect. It does not explain why the constants have the values they have. It explains why we should not be surprised to find ourselves in a universe where those values permit our existence.

The strong anthropic principle asserts that the universe must have properties that allow life to develop at some stage. The final anthropic principle adds that information processing, once begun, will continue forever. Neither claim follows from the weak principle. Both go beyond the evidence. The weak principle is a reminder about sampling. The others are conjectures.

Hoyle predicted a resonance in carbon-12 that allows the triple-alpha process to proceed in stars. The resonance was found. The prediction is sometimes cited as an anthropic success. It was a nuclear-physics calculation guided by the requirement that carbon be produced. The requirement is empirical. Carbon exists. The calculation showed where the resonance had to lie. The episode illustrates how the existence of a known outcome can constrain an unknown parameter. It does not demonstrate that the parameter was chosen for that outcome.

The constants may be fixed by a more fundamental theory. They may vary across a multiverse, with observers appearing only in the compatible regions. Both possibilities are open. The anthropic observation records the compatibility. It does not decide the mechanism. The observation remains: the universe we inhabit is one in which the constants allow chemistry, stars, and observers. That fact is not in dispute. Its explanation is.

title: Orders of Magnitude from the Constants
paras: Many characteristic sizes and energies in physics follow from the fundamental constants by dimensional analysis. The Bohr radius is \( a_0 = \hbar^2 / (m_e e^2) \). Atomic densities are then of order \( m_N / a_0^3 \), a few grams per cubic centimeter for light elements. The result matches the densities of ordinary solids and liquids.

Nuclear sizes follow from the range of the strong force. The pion Compton wavelength sets that range at about 1.4 femtometers. The binding energy per nucleon is a few MeV. The same constants that fix atomic sizes fix nuclear sizes once the strong coupling is given. The ratio of the two scales is large because the strong force is strong and short-range while electromagnetism is weaker and long-range.

Stellar masses and lifetimes are constrained by the same constants. A self-gravitating body of atomic density reaches a central temperature set by the balance of gravitational compression and electron degeneracy pressure. For the temperature to ignite hydrogen fusion the mass must lie in a range that produces main-sequence stars. The main-sequence lifetime is then fixed by the nuclear energy release and the luminosity. The Sun’s lifetime is long enough for planetary evolution and short enough that the universe is still young when the first such stars appear. Both facts follow from the constants once the requirement of stable nuclear burning is imposed.

Planetary atmospheres are retained only when the escape velocity exceeds the thermal speed of the gas at temperatures where liquid water or complex chemistry can exist. Bodies much smaller than Earth lose their atmospheres. Bodies much larger become gas giants. The window is set by gravity, temperature, and molecular mass. The existence of rocky planets with atmospheres is therefore a consequence of the same constants that permit stars and chemistry.

These relations do not require the anthropic principle. They are ordinary dimensional consequences of the measured constants. The anthropic observation is that the constants permit the relations to produce long-lived stars, rocky planets, and carbon chemistry at the same epoch. The dimensional results stand independently. They show how little freedom the constants leave once they are fixed.

title: Cell Theory and Germ Theory
paras: The cell theory states that all living organisms are composed of cells and that cells arise only from pre-existing cells. The statement was assembled in the nineteenth century from observations by Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow. It replaced earlier views that living matter could arise spontaneously or that tissues were continuous substances. Every organism examined since has confirmed the rule. Viruses are not cells, but they replicate only inside cells.

The germ theory states that many diseases are caused by microorganisms. Pasteur’s experiments on fermentation and putrefaction, and Koch’s isolation of specific pathogens, established the link. The same organisms that cause disease can be cultured, identified, and, in many cases, killed or blocked. Antisepsis, antibiotics, and vaccines followed. The theory does not claim that every illness is infectious. It claims that infectious illnesses have microbial causes that can be demonstrated.

Both theories are now foundational. Cell theory organizes development, physiology, and evolution. Germ theory organizes public health and medicine. Neither required a new force. Both followed from the consistent application of microscopy, staining, and controlled experiment. The results are independent of the particular wording in which they were first announced. The observations remain.

title: Mendel and the Chromosomes
paras: Gregor Mendel crossed pea plants that differed in clear traits and counted the offspring. Tall crossed with dwarf gave all tall in the first generation. Self-pollination of those hybrids gave three tall to one dwarf in the next. The dwarf trait had not disappeared. It had been hidden. Mendel proposed that each plant carries two factors for each trait, that the factors separate when gametes form, and that one factor can mask the other. The ratios followed. The same pattern held for other traits he tested.

The factors are now called genes. They are segments of DNA. The separation Mendel inferred is the separation of homologous chromosomes in meiosis. Each gamete receives one member of each pair. Fertilization restores the pair. The masking is dominance. The hidden factor is recessive. When both copies are recessive the trait appears. The arithmetic is the same whether the factors are abstract or molecular.

The work was published in 1866 and ignored. It was rediscovered in 1900 by investigators who had reached the same ratios. Within a few years the factors were located on chromosomes. Sutton and Boveri noted that chromosomes behave as Mendel’s factors must behave. Morgan’s group in fruit flies mapped genes to specific positions by measuring how often traits are inherited together. Linkage and recombination became measurable. The chromosome theory of inheritance was established.

The theory accounts for the transmission of traits. It does not by itself account for the origin of new traits. That required the later recognition of mutation. Together, Mendelian transmission and mutational variation supplied the genetic mechanism that Darwin’s theory had lacked. The mechanism is now molecular. The ratios Mendel counted remain.

title: Microbiology
paras: Microbiology is the study of organisms too small to see without magnification. The group includes bacteria, archaea, many fungi, protists, and viruses. Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes. They lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Their DNA is a circular chromosome in the cytoplasm, often accompanied by smaller plasmids. Eukaryotic microbes have nuclei and organelles.

Bacteria reproduce by binary fission. Under favorable conditions some species double in twenty minutes. They exchange genes by transformation, transduction, and conjugation. These processes move DNA between cells that are not parent and offspring. The result is rapid spread of traits, including antibiotic resistance.

Archaea resemble bacteria in size and simplicity but differ in membrane lipids, cell-wall chemistry, and the machinery of transcription and translation. Many live in extremes of temperature, salinity, or acidity. Some produce methane. Their ribosomal RNA sequences place them on a separate branch of the tree of life.

Fungi and protists are eukaryotes. Yeasts are unicellular fungi used in fermentation. Molds form filaments. Protists include algae that photosynthesize and protozoa that ingest food. Amoebae are protists that move and feed by extending temporary projections of cytoplasm called pseudopods. The projections form by local changes in the cytoskeleton. The cell crawls toward food or away from harm. Some amoebae are free-living in soil and water. Others are parasitic.

Microbes drive the major chemical cycles of the planet. They fix nitrogen, produce oxygen, decompose organic matter, and generate methane. They also cause disease. The same tools—culture, microscopy, staining, and sequencing—identify both the beneficial and the pathogenic species. The distinction is ecological, not taxonomic.

title: Viruses
paras: Viruses are particles that replicate only inside living cells. They consist of nucleic acid enclosed in a protein coat. Some have a lipid envelope derived from the host membrane. The nucleic acid is DNA or RNA, single- or double-stranded, linear or circular. The coat protects the genome and, in many cases, attaches to a receptor on the host cell.

Outside a cell a virus is inert. It has no metabolism and no independent replication. Inside a susceptible cell it redirects the host machinery to copy its genome and synthesize its proteins. New particles assemble and leave, often destroying the cell. The host range is limited by the receptors the virus can bind. A virus that infects one species may be unable to infect another.

Bacteriophages infect bacteria. They were used to show that DNA, not protein, carries genetic information. Animal and plant viruses cause many diseases. Some insert their genome into the host chromosome and remain latent. Others kill the cell quickly. Retroviruses reverse-transcribe RNA into DNA that integrates into the host genome. The integrated form can be transmitted to daughter cells.

Viruses evolve. Mutation rates are high, especially in RNA viruses. Recombination and reassortment occur when multiple viruses infect the same cell. The result is rapid change in surface proteins and in host range. Vaccines and antiviral drugs select for resistant variants. The same processes that generate diversity in cellular organisms operate, at higher speed, in viruses.

Viruses are not classified as living by most definitions because they lack independent metabolism. They are biological entities that evolve and that affect every domain of life. They move genes between hosts, regulate microbial populations, and shape the evolution of immune systems. Their study is part of microbiology whether or not they are counted as organisms.

title: Amoebae
paras: Amoebae are unicellular eukaryotes that move by pseudopods. The pseudopod is a temporary extension of the cytoplasm. Actin filaments polymerize at the leading edge and push the membrane forward. Myosin and other motors contract at the rear. The cell advances. The same machinery is used for phagocytosis. The amoeba surrounds a particle of food, encloses it in a vesicle, and digests it with enzymes delivered from lysosomes.

Most amoebae are free-living. They inhabit soil, fresh water, and marine sediments. They feed on bacteria, algae, and detritus. A few species are parasitic. Entamoeba histolytica infects the human intestine and can invade the liver. Naegleria fowleri is free-living in warm water and can infect the brain if it enters through the nose. These cases are rare. Most amoebae never encounter a human host.

Amoebae were among the first microbes observed. Leeuwenhoek described them in the seventeenth century. Later workers used them to study cell movement, phagocytosis, and cytoplasmic streaming. The mechanisms proved to be general. The same actin–myosin system operates in the white blood cells of animals and in the crawling of many other cells. The amoeba is a convenient model because the entire organism is one cell and the behavior is visible under a light microscope.

The group is not a single evolutionary lineage. “Amoeba” describes a body plan that has evolved more than once. Some amoeboid organisms are closely related to animals and fungi. Others belong to distant branches of the eukaryotic tree. The shared appearance is convergent. The underlying cell biology is ancient.

title: Modern DNA Methods
paras: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences. DNA ligase joins the ends. The combination allowed recombinant DNA in the 1970s. A gene from one organism could be inserted into a plasmid and propagated in bacteria. The technique produced insulin, growth hormone, and many other proteins.

The polymerase chain reaction amplifies a chosen segment of DNA exponentially. A pair of primers, a heat-stable polymerase, and thermal cycling generate millions of copies from a few molecules. Sequencing reads the order of bases. Sanger sequencing used chain-terminating nucleotides. Next-generation methods read millions of fragments in parallel. A human genome that once required years and hundreds of millions of dollars can now be sequenced in hours for hundreds of dollars.

CRISPR-Cas systems are adaptive immune mechanisms in bacteria. A guide RNA directs the Cas nuclease to a matching DNA sequence. The nuclease cuts. The cell repairs the break. Repair can disable the gene or, if a template is supplied, insert a new sequence. Base editors and prime editors change single bases or short stretches without double-strand breaks. The tools work in bacteria, plants, animals, and human cells. They are used in research, in agriculture, and in clinical trials for genetic disease.

Gene drives bias inheritance so that a chosen allele spreads through a population faster than Mendelian ratios allow. They have been demonstrated in insects in the laboratory. Their use outside containment is contested because the spread is designed to be difficult to reverse.

The methods are precise relative to earlier mutagenesis. They are not perfectly precise. Off-target cuts occur. Delivery to the right cells in a living organism remains difficult. The capability to read, write, and edit DNA at scale now exists. The limits are technical, regulatory, and ethical.

title: Cloning
paras: Cloning produces a genetic copy of an organism. In plants it is routine. Cuttings and tissue culture generate identical individuals. In animals the method is somatic-cell nuclear transfer. The nucleus of a somatic cell is placed in an enucleated egg. The reconstructed egg is stimulated to develop. The resulting animal has the nuclear genome of the donor.

Dolly the sheep was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell. She was born in 1996. The success rate was low. Many reconstructed embryos failed. Those that developed sometimes showed abnormalities. Subsequent work produced cloned cattle, pigs, goats, cats, dogs, and other species. Efficiency has improved but remains far below natural reproduction.

In 2018 Chinese researchers produced the first cloned primates, two macaques, from fetal fibroblasts. A later rhesus monkey was cloned from fetal cells and required a non-cloned placenta. No healthy primate has been produced from an adult somatic cell. The reprogramming of an adult nucleus is incomplete in primates under current methods.

Reproductive cloning of humans has not been achieved. No verified human clone has been born. Therapeutic cloning, the production of embryonic stem cells genetically matched to a patient, has been performed in the laboratory. The embryos are not implanted. Most countries prohibit reproductive human cloning. A smaller number permit research on cloned human embryos under license. The technical barrier in primates remains high. The regulatory barrier is explicit.

title: Human Genetics
paras: The human genome contains about three billion base pairs and roughly twenty thousand protein-coding genes. Most of the sequence does not code for protein. Regulatory elements, introns, and repetitive DNA make up the majority. Variation among individuals is about one difference per thousand bases. Most variants are neutral. A minority affect traits or disease risk.

Monogenic disorders are caused by variants in a single gene. Sickle-cell disease, cystic fibrosis, and Huntington’s disease are examples. The inheritance follows Mendelian ratios when the variant is fully penetrant. Many common diseases are polygenic. Height, blood pressure, and susceptibility to type 2 diabetes or schizophrenia are influenced by thousands of variants of small effect, plus environment. Polygenic scores sum the effects. They are predictive in populations similar to the ones in which they were derived and less predictive in others.

Genome-wide association studies scan hundreds of thousands of people for statistical links between variants and traits. The links identify regions. They do not by themselves prove causation. Functional studies are required. The same methods have mapped genes that affect drug response, a field called pharmacogenetics. A variant that is harmless in one context can determine whether a drug is effective or toxic.

Editing the human germline changes DNA that can be inherited. In 2018 He Jiankui announced the birth of twins whose embryos had been edited at the CCR5 locus. The work was widely condemned. He was convicted in China of illegal medical practice and imprisoned. Chinese regulations now prohibit clinical research that alters germ cells or embryos for reproduction. Somatic editing, which affects only the treated individual, is in clinical trials for several diseases. The distinction between somatic and germline alteration is the current regulatory boundary.

title: Optics and Quantum Mechanics
paras: Classical optics treats light as a wave. Interference, diffraction, and polarization follow from the wave equation. The speed in vacuum is \( c \). In a medium it is \( c/n \), where \( n \) is the refractive index. Lenses and mirrors redirect rays according to the law of reflection and Snell’s law of refraction. These rules are exact in the geometric-optics limit and are recovered as the short-wavelength limit of the wave theory.

Quantum mechanics assigns an amplitude to each path a photon can take. The probability is the square of the sum of the amplitudes. The same rule produces the interference pattern in a double-slit experiment when single photons are sent one at a time. The photon is detected at one place. The pattern builds from many detections. No trajectory is observed between source and detector. The calculation uses every path.

The photoelectric effect and Compton scattering show that light delivers energy and momentum in discrete quanta. The energy of a photon is \( E = h\nu \). The momentum is \( E/c \). These relations are confirmed by the threshold frequencies of photoemission and by the wavelength shift in Compton scattering. The wave and particle descriptions are complementary. Each is exact in its domain. Neither is complete alone.

Quantum electrodynamics unifies the two. The electromagnetic field is quantized. Photons are its quanta. Electrons interact by exchanging virtual photons. The theory reproduces classical optics in the appropriate limit and adds the quantum corrections measured in the Lamb shift and the anomalous magnetic moment. Optics is the classical limit of quantum electrodynamics. The underlying rules are quantum.

title: Unified Theories
paras: Maxwell’s equations unified electricity, magnetism, and light. The electroweak theory unified the electromagnetic and weak forces. At energies above roughly 100 GeV the two forces are aspects of a single interaction. Below that scale the Higgs mechanism gives mass to the W and Z bosons and leaves the photon massless. The strong force is described by quantum chromodynamics. It has not been unified with the electroweak force in a confirmed theory.

Grand unified theories embed the strong, weak, and electromagnetic forces in a single gauge group. They predict that the three couplings meet at a high energy and that the proton is unstable. The meeting of the couplings is approximate in the simplest models. Proton decay has not been observed. The experimental lower limit on the proton lifetime exceeds the predictions of the minimal theories. More elaborate models remain possible. None is confirmed.

Gravity is described by general relativity, a classical theory of curved spacetime. No quantum theory of gravity is established. String theory and loop quantum gravity are research programs. Neither has made a confirmed prediction that distinguishes it from the others or from general relativity plus the Standard Model. The Standard Model plus general relativity accounts for all confirmed particle-physics and gravitational phenomena. The unification of gravity with the other forces remains open.

The pattern of past unifications is clear. Phenomena once thought distinct were shown to be aspects of a single framework. The framework then made new predictions. The same pattern is sought for the remaining forces. It has not yet been completed.

title: The Expansion of the Universe
paras: Galaxies recede from one another. The recession velocity is proportional to distance for nearby galaxies. The constant of proportionality is the Hubble constant. Its present value is approximately 70 kilometers per second per megaparsec, with a tension of several kilometers per second per megaparsec between local and cosmic-microwave-background determinations. The expansion is observed in every direction. It is not an explosion from a center in space. It is an increase in the scale of space itself.

The expansion stretches the wavelength of light traveling through it. Distant galaxies appear redder. The same stretching cools the cosmic microwave background. The background is the cooled remnant of the hot early universe. Its spectrum is thermal. Its temperature is 2.725 kelvin. Small anisotropies in the temperature map the density fluctuations that later grew into galaxies.

The expansion rate has not been constant. It slowed under the influence of matter for most of cosmic history. In the last few billion years it has accelerated. The acceleration is attributed to a component whose pressure is negative. That component is called dark energy. Its density is roughly constant with expansion. Matter density falls. Dark energy therefore comes to dominate. The transition occurred when the universe was about half its present age.

The expansion implies a finite age. Extrapolating backward under the observed contents yields an age of about 13.8 billion years. The figure is consistent with the ages of the oldest stars and with the cooling time of the microwave background. The universe has a history. The history is readable in the redshifts, the background radiation, and the abundances of the light elements.

title: Dark Matter
paras: Galaxies rotate faster in their outer regions than the visible mass can explain. Clusters of galaxies bend light and bind hot gas more strongly than their luminous matter allows. The cosmic microwave background shows acoustic peaks whose positions require additional non-baryonic matter. These observations converge on a component that gravitates but does not emit, absorb, or scatter light at detectable levels. It is called dark matter.

The density of dark matter is about five times the density of ordinary matter. It is cold, meaning that its particles moved slowly when structures formed. Cold dark matter collapses into halos. Ordinary matter falls into the halos and forms galaxies. The halos are larger than the visible galaxies. Their presence is inferred from rotation curves, gravitational lensing, and the growth of structure.

No dark-matter particle has been detected in the laboratory. Candidates include weakly interacting massive particles, axions, and sterile neutrinos. Direct-detection experiments set limits on the scattering cross-section. Indirect searches look for annihilation products. Collider searches look for missing energy. None has produced a confirmed signal. The gravitational evidence remains. The identity of the matter does not.

Modified-gravity theories attempt to explain the observations without new particles. They reproduce some galactic rotation curves. They have greater difficulty with clusters, with the microwave background, and with the separation of mass and light in merging clusters. The dark-matter hypothesis accounts for all of these with one additional component. It is the working description. It is not yet a completed identification.

title: Dark Energy
paras: The expansion of the universe is accelerating. Type Ia supernovae at high redshift are fainter than they would be in a decelerating universe. The microwave-background acoustic peaks and the large-scale distribution of galaxies independently require a component that drives acceleration. The component has negative pressure. Its energy density is roughly constant as the universe expands. It is called dark energy.

The simplest model is a cosmological constant. Einstein introduced the term to permit a static universe. It was later set to zero. The observations revive it with a small positive value. The constant corresponds to an energy density of about \( 10^{-29} \) grams per cubic centimeter. Quantum field theory predicts a far larger vacuum energy. The discrepancy is many orders of magnitude. No accepted resolution exists.

Other models allow the density to vary slowly. They are parameterized by an equation-of-state index \( w \). Current data are consistent with \( w = -1 \), the value for a cosmological constant, to within a few percent. Future surveys of supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and weak lensing will tighten the constraint. A clear departure from \( -1 \) would rule out the simplest model.

Dark energy dominates the present energy budget. It did not dominate in the past. Its presence sets the ultimate fate of the expansion. If it remains constant, the expansion continues forever and galaxies beyond the local group eventually leave the observable universe. The inference rests on the measured acceleration and on the assumption that the component persists. Both are supported by present data. Both remain open to revision.

title: Hubble and Webb
paras: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990 into low Earth orbit. Its primary mirror is 2.4 meters in diameter. It observes from the near-ultraviolet to the near-infrared. Servicing missions corrected its optics and replaced instruments. It has measured the expansion rate, imaged distant galaxies, and resolved disks around young stars.

The James Webb Space Telescope was launched in 2021 and operates at the Sun–Earth L2 point, 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. Its primary mirror is 6.5 meters across, composed of 18 gold-coated beryllium segments. A five-layer sunshield keeps the telescope near 40 kelvin. Webb observes from the red visible to the mid-infrared. The longer wavelengths penetrate dust and reach the redshifted light of the first galaxies.

Webb’s collecting area is more than five times Hubble’s. Its infrared sensitivity reveals galaxies that formed within a few hundred million years after the Big Bang, the atmospheres of exoplanets by transmission spectroscopy, and the interiors of star-forming clouds. Hubble continues to provide ultraviolet and optical coverage. The two telescopes are complementary. Together they span the electromagnetic spectrum from the ultraviolet to the mid-infrared and the cosmic timeline from the present to the first luminous objects.

title: Andromeda and Alpha Centauri
paras: The Andromeda galaxy is the nearest large spiral to the Milky Way. It lies about 2.5 million light-years away. It contains roughly a trillion stars and is approaching the Milky Way at about 110 kilometers per second. The two galaxies are expected to merge in roughly four billion years. Andromeda has its own satellite galaxies and a supermassive black hole at its center. No individual planets have been resolved there. The distance precludes detailed spectroscopy of Earth-sized worlds with present instruments.

Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system to the Sun, 4.37 light-years away. It is a triple system. Alpha Centauri A and B are Sun-like stars that orbit each other. Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf that orbits the pair at a greater distance. Proxima has at least one confirmed planet, Proxima b, with a minimum mass near that of Earth and an orbital period of about 11 days. The planet lies in the star’s habitable zone, where liquid water could exist on the surface if the atmosphere is suitable. The star is active. Flares and high-energy radiation may erode atmospheres. No atmosphere has been detected. The system is the closest place where an Earth-sized planet in a temperate orbit is known to exist. Whether that planet retains water or supports life is unknown.

title: The Moons of Jupiter and Possible Habitats
paras: Jupiter has four large moons. Io is volcanically active. Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto have icy surfaces. Europa and Ganymede show evidence of subsurface oceans. Europa’s ocean is global, salty, and in contact with a rocky seafloor. Tidal flexing from Jupiter supplies heat. The ice shell is kilometers to tens of kilometers thick. Plumes of water vapor have been reported. The surface is bombarded by radiation from Jupiter’s magnetosphere. Any life would have to exist in the ocean, powered by chemical energy rather than sunlight.

Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System. It has its own magnetic field and a subsurface ocean sandwiched between layers of ice. The ocean is farther from the rocky interior than Europa’s. Chemical exchange with rock is less certain. Callisto may also have a deep ocean, but the evidence is weaker and the heat flux is lower.

Saturn’s moon Enceladus ejects plumes of water vapor, ice grains, salts, and organic molecules from its south polar region. The plumes are fed by a subsurface ocean. Cassini measured molecular hydrogen in the plumes, consistent with hydrothermal activity on the seafloor. The ocean is alkaline. Laboratory experiments show that some Earth methanogens can grow under similar conditions. No life has been detected. The ingredients that support metabolism on Earth—liquid water, chemical energy, and organic compounds—are present.

These moons are the strongest candidates for present-day habitable environments beyond Earth. They have liquid water and energy sources. They lack confirmed biosignatures. Future missions that sample the plumes or penetrate the ice will test whether the chemistry has remained abiotic or has crossed into biology.

title: Black Holes
paras: A black hole is a region of spacetime from which no signal can reach distant observers. The boundary of the region is the event horizon. In the Schwarzschild solution the horizon lies at the radius \( r_s = 2GM/c^2 \). For a solar-mass object the radius is 3 km. Inside the horizon every future-directed path ends at the central singularity.

Astrophysical black holes form by the collapse of massive stellar cores and by the subsequent growth of those seeds through accretion and mergers. Stellar-mass black holes are observed as X-ray binaries and as the sources of gravitational-wave signals. Supermassive black holes, millions to billions of solar masses, occupy the centres of most large galaxies. The Event Horizon Telescope has imaged the shadows of the black holes in M87 and in the Milky Way; the measured diameters match the general-relativistic prediction.

Matter falling toward a black hole forms an accretion disk. Viscous transport of angular momentum allows the gas to spiral inward, converting gravitational potential energy into heat and radiation. The efficiency can exceed 10 percent of the rest mass for a rapidly rotating hole—higher than nuclear fusion. The same disks power quasars and many galactic X-ray sources.

The classical theory predicts that the horizon area never decreases and that the surface gravity is constant over the horizon. When quantum field theory is included, the horizon emits thermal radiation at the Hawking temperature \( \hbar c^3/(8\pi GMk_B) \). The radiation carries the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy \( k_Bc^3A/(4G\hbar) \). Complete evaporation of an initially pure state appears to produce a mixed state, raising the information paradox. Recent calculations in simplified models suggest that unitarity is preserved, but no consensus mechanism yet exists for realistic black holes.
No observation contradicts the general-relativistic description of the exterior. The interior, the singularity, and the ultimate fate of the information remain outside present experimental reach.

title: Wormholes
paras: A wormhole is a hypothetical tunnel connecting two distant regions of spacetime. In the simplest mathematical models the tunnel is held open by matter that violates the null energy condition. Ordinary matter does not. Quantum fields can violate the condition locally and briefly. Whether they can do so on the scale and for the duration needed to keep a macroscopic wormhole open is unknown.

No wormhole has been observed. General relativity permits the solutions. It does not require them. Traversable wormholes would allow shortcuts between distant points and, in some arrangements, closed timelike curves. Closed timelike curves permit paths that return to the same event. They raise consistency problems. Proposals that prevent their formation or that render them unstable exist. None is confirmed.

The existence of wormholes is therefore an open question in classical and quantum gravity. They are not required by any confirmed observation. They are not forbidden by the present form of the field equations when exotic matter is allowed. Until a quantum theory of gravity is established, or until an observation demands them, they remain mathematical possibilities without empirical support.

title: The Fabric of Spacetime
paras: Spacetime is the four-dimensional manifold whose geometry is determined by the distribution of energy and momentum. The Einstein field equation relates the curvature of spacetime to the stress-energy tensor. In the absence of mass and energy the geometry is flat. In their presence it is curved. Freely falling objects follow geodesics of that geometry. The curvature is what is measured as gravity.

The geometry is dynamic. It changes when matter moves. Gravitational waves are ripples in the geometry that propagate at the speed of light. They have been detected from merging black holes and neutron stars. The waves carry energy and momentum. Their existence confirms that spacetime is not a fixed background. It is a physical field.

At ordinary scales the geometry is smooth. At the Planck scale, about \( 10^{-35} \) meters, quantum effects are expected to dominate. The classical description fails. Candidate theories replace the smooth manifold with discrete structures, strings, or other entities. None has been confirmed. The successful description from laboratory scales to cosmological scales remains the smooth geometry of general relativity coupled to the Standard Model of particle physics.
The fabric is therefore the geometry itself. It is shaped by what it contains. It propagates waves. It has a classical limit that is extraordinarily accurate. Its quantum completion is unknown.

title: Time Reversal
paras: The fundamental equations of classical mechanics, electromagnetism, and quantum mechanics are invariant under reversal of the time coordinate. If a sequence of events is allowed, the time-reversed sequence is also a solution. The equations do not prefer one direction.

The observed universe does. Entropy increases. Heat flows from hot to cold. Memory records the past, not the future. The asymmetry is statistical. A system that begins in a low-entropy state is overwhelmingly likely to evolve toward higher entropy. The early universe was in such a state. The microwave background and the smoothness of the large-scale geometry record that fact. Why the initial entropy was low is not explained by the time-symmetric equations.

Weak interactions violate time-reversal symmetry by a small amount. The violation has been measured in the decays of neutral kaons and B mesons. It is required by the observed excess of matter over antimatter. The effect is tiny. It does not account for the thermodynamic arrow. The thermodynamic arrow is explained by the initial condition, not by a fundamental asymmetry in the microscopic laws.

Time reversal is therefore a symmetry of the equations and a broken symmetry of the solutions we inhabit. The equations permit both directions. The universe we observe has a past boundary of low entropy and a future of higher entropy. The origin of that boundary remains an open question in cosmology.

title: Entropy
paras: Entropy is a measure of the number of microscopic arrangements that correspond to a given macroscopic state. A system with many accessible microstates has high entropy. A system with few has low entropy. The second law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of an isolated system does not decrease. It stays the same in reversible processes and increases in irreversible ones.

The law is statistical. Every microstate is equally likely. There are vastly more microstates that look disordered than microstates that look ordered. A system that begins in a low-entropy state is therefore overwhelmingly likely to evolve toward higher entropy. The reverse evolution is not forbidden. It is improbable to a degree that makes it unobservable in ordinary systems.

Heat flows from hot to cold because the combined system has more microstates when the temperatures are equal. Gases expand to fill their containers because the expanded state has more arrangements. Living organisms maintain low internal entropy by exporting entropy to their surroundings. The total entropy of organism plus surroundings still rises. The Sun’s increase in entropy supplies the margin that allows the decrease on Earth.

The early universe was in a state of remarkably low entropy. The microwave background is smooth to one part in a hundred thousand. That smoothness is a low-entropy condition for the gravitational field. The subsequent increase in entropy includes the formation of stars, galaxies, and black holes. Black holes have entropy proportional to the area of their event horizons. They dominate the entropy budget of the observable universe.

Entropy defines a direction in time. The microscopic equations are time-symmetric. The boundary condition of low entropy in the past is not. The second law is the macroscopic consequence of that boundary condition. Why the boundary condition was low remains unexplained.

title: Maxwell’s Demon
paras: Maxwell imagined a being that could sort molecules. A partition divides a box of gas. A small door in the partition is operated by the demon. When a fast molecule approaches from the left, the demon opens the door. When a slow molecule approaches, the demon leaves it closed. The right side grows hotter. The left side grows colder. Entropy appears to decrease without work being done. The second law seems violated.

The resolution is that the demon must acquire information. Measuring the speed of a molecule requires a physical interaction. The interaction increases the entropy of the measuring apparatus by at least as much as the entropy decrease in the gas. When the demon’s memory is erased to make room for the next measurement, the erasure dissipates heat. The total entropy of gas plus demon plus surroundings does not fall. The second law holds.

The argument was made precise by Szilard, Landauer, and Bennett. Landauer’s principle states that erasing one bit of information in a system at temperature \( T \) dissipates at least \( kT \ln 2 \) of heat. The principle has been tested in small systems. The measured dissipation matches the bound. Information is physical. Its acquisition and erasure have thermodynamic costs.

The demon does not refute the second law. It illustrates that the law applies to the complete system, including whatever performs the measurement and the erasure. No known process sorts molecules in a way that reduces the entropy of an isolated system. The thought experiment remains useful because it forces the accounting to be complete.

title: The Direction of Time
paras: The microscopic laws of physics are invariant under time reversal. If a process is allowed, the time-reversed process is also a solution of the equations. Classical mechanics, electromagnetism, and the Schrödinger equation share this symmetry. The weak interaction violates it by a small, measured amount. The violation is insufficient to produce the observed arrow.

The thermodynamic arrow points from low entropy to high entropy. The early universe was gravitationally smooth and thermally uniform. That state has low entropy. Subsequent evolution increases entropy through the formation of structure, the burning of stars, and the growth of black holes. Memory, causation, and the psychological sense of passage align with this gradient. Records exist of the past because the past was the low-entropy boundary.

No fundamental law forbids the opposite gradient. A universe that began in a high-entropy state would not develop a consistent arrow. The existence of the arrow is therefore a fact about the boundary condition, not about the dynamical laws. Why the boundary condition was low-entropy remains an open question in cosmology. Proposals include special initial conditions, inflationary smoothing, and selection effects. None is established.

title: The Block Universe
paras: The block-universe view treats spacetime as a four-dimensional whole. Every event—past, present, and future—exists in the manifold. The passage of time is not an additional physical process. It is the relation between events ordered by the metric. An observer’s experience of “now” is the set of events on one spacelike surface. Different observers have different surfaces. None is privileged by the geometry.

The view is compatible with special and general relativity. The relativity of simultaneity already denies a universal present. The block description simply extends that denial to the entire history. Deterministic equations reinforce the picture: the solution on the whole manifold is fixed by data on any Cauchy surface. Stochastic equations replace a single block with a measure over blocks. In either case the fundamental object is the spacetime, not a moving present.

The view does not deny change. Change is the difference between events at different times. It denies that change requires a meta-time in which the present advances. The denial is metaphysical. Physics supplies the metric and the field equations. It does not supply an additional flowing now. Whether the block description is the correct ontology is not settled by experiment. It is a consistent reading of the existing formalism.

title: Time as a Parameter
paras: In ordinary quantum mechanics and in classical field theory, time is a parameter, not an operator. The state evolves with respect to an external time. Position is an operator. Momentum is an operator. Time is the variable that labels the evolution. There is no time operator conjugate to the Hamiltonian that satisfies the canonical commutation relation on the full Hilbert space. Pauli showed that a self-adjoint time operator bounded below by the spectrum of the Hamiltonian cannot exist.

The parameter status is unproblematic in non-gravitational physics. Clocks exist. They are physical systems whose readings correlate with the parameter. The correlations are reliable. The underlying equations remain parameterized by an external t.

In canonical quantum gravity the situation changes. The Hamiltonian constraint generates evolution. There is no external time. The Wheeler–DeWitt equation is timeless. Solutions are static wave functionals on the space of geometries. Time must be recovered, if at all, as a relation among the degrees of freedom. Different choices of internal clock yield different approximate Schrödinger equations. The recovery is approximate and contingent on the existence of suitable semiclassical degrees of freedom.

Time is therefore fundamental in the sense that the non-gravitational theories are written in terms of it, and emergent in the sense that a quantum theory of the gravitational field may not contain it as a basic variable. Both descriptions are in use. Neither has been shown to be the final one.

title: Complex Time
paras: The Schrödinger equation is first-order in time and contains the imaginary unit. The formal substitution \( t \to -i\tau \) converts it into a diffusion equation. The substitution is useful in calculations. Euclidean path integrals rotate the time contour to make the action positive and the integral convergent. Instanton methods and lattice gauge theory rely on the rotation. The rotation is a mathematical device. It does not imply that physical time is complex.

Some proposals in quantum gravity and in the study of the wave function of the universe treat the early universe as Euclidean and the later universe as Lorentzian. The signature of the metric changes. The change is a feature of particular minisuperspace models. It is not required by a general theory. No observation demands complex time coordinates.

Complex spacetime appears in twistor theory and in some string-theory constructions. The constructions are equivalent, in their physical predictions, to ordinary real spacetime plus additional structure. They do not alter the measured reality of real time intervals. Clocks still advance along real world-lines. The use of complex variables simplifies certain calculations. It does not replace the real parameter that orders events in the laboratory.

title: It from Bit
paras: Wheeler proposed that every physical entity derives its significance from answers to yes-or-no questions. The slogan is “it from bit.” A particle, a field, or a region of spacetime acquires its properties through the registration of binary outcomes by measuring apparatus. The proposal does not claim that information replaces the field equations. It claims that the meaning of the physical quantities is fixed by the information those quantities yield under interrogation.

The idea draws on the structure of quantum mechanics. A measurement yields a definite result from a set of possible results. The result is recorded. Subsequent predictions use the updated state. Wheeler elevated the recording step from an epistemic convenience to an ontological primitive. Whether the elevation is required by the formalism is disputed. The formalism works with or without it. The proposal remains an interpretation.

Quantum information theory has since shown that information-theoretic constraints reproduce parts of quantum mechanics. No-cloning, no-deletion, and the existence of entanglement follow from simple axioms about information. These results are consistent with the spirit of the slogan. They do not demonstrate that spacetime or the metric emerges from bits. That demonstration is still absent.

title: The Participatory Universe
paras: Wheeler argued that the observer is a participator. The act of measurement is not a passive registration of a pre-existing value. It is an intervention that elicits one outcome from a set of possibilities. The universe, on this view, does not sit finished and independent of all acts of observation. Its definite properties are brought about, in part, by those acts.

The delayed-choice experiment illustrates the claim. A photon passes through a double slit. After it has passed, the experimenter chooses whether to measure which-path information or an interference pattern. The choice appears to determine whether the photon behaved as a particle or as a wave in the apparatus it has already traversed. The quantum calculation accounts for the statistics without assigning a trajectory. Wheeler read the result as evidence that the past is not fixed until the measurement is completed.

The reading is optional. The standard formalism predicts the same correlations whether or not one speaks of participation. No experiment has shown that a conscious observer is required. Apparatus alone suffices. The participatory language emphasizes that measurement outcomes are not revealed properties of a detached system. It does not alter the predictive rules. The rules remain those of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Foam
paras: Wheeler suggested that spacetime at the Planck scale is not smooth. Geometry fluctuates. The fluctuations are large enough that the classical manifold description fails. He called the fluctuating geometry quantum foam. Virtual black holes, wormholes, and changes of topology appear and disappear on timescales of the Planck time. The average geometry over larger scales remains the smooth spacetime of general relativity.

No direct observation of the foam exists. Particle accelerators reach energies many orders of magnitude below the Planck energy. Indirect limits come from the absence of certain effects that large fluctuations would produce: dispersion of light from distant sources, or violations of Lorentz invariance. The limits constrain the size of the fluctuations but do not rule out a foamy structure at the Planck length.

The idea is a qualitative expectation from combining general relativity and quantum mechanics. A full quantum theory of gravity would replace the expectation with a definite spectrum of fluctuations or with a different microstructure. Until that theory exists, quantum foam remains a plausible picture of the short-distance regime and an untested one.

title: Hawking Radiation
paras: Hawking radiation is the thermal flux emitted by a black hole. It arises when quantum fields propagate on the curved spacetime of a collapsing body. Modes that straddle the horizon become entangled. The exterior member of each pair escapes to infinity as a real particle. The spectrum seen by a distant observer is thermal at the temperature
\[ T = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G M k_B}. \]

The temperature is inversely proportional to the mass. A solar-mass hole radiates at about \( 10^{-7} \) K, far below the cosmic microwave background. A hole of mass \( 10^{12} \) kg radiates at room temperature and evaporates on a timescale comparable to the age of the universe. The power scales as \( 1/M^2 \). Evaporation therefore accelerates as the hole shrinks.

The radiation carries energy, angular momentum and charge. It reduces the mass of the hole. When the mass approaches the Planck mass the semi-classical calculation ceases to be reliable. The final stage of evaporation is unknown. The existence of the radiation follows from the structure of the vacuum in curved spacetime and from the presence of a horizon. It has not been observed directly. Its theoretical necessity is nevertheless required for the consistency of black-hole thermodynamics with the ordinary second law.

title: The Black-Hole Information Question
paras: Hawking radiation is thermal. A thermal spectrum is determined by temperature alone. It contains no information about the matter that formed the black hole. If the hole evaporates completely, the information appears to be lost. Quantum mechanics requires unitary evolution. Information should be preserved. The conflict is the information question.

Hawking initially concluded that information is destroyed. Later calculations and the AdS/CFT correspondence suggested that it is preserved. The radiation is not exactly thermal.
