paras: Anomalies are symmetries of the classical action that are broken by quantum effects. The chiral anomaly is the non-conservation of the axial current in the presence of gauge fields. It is required for the decay of the neutral pion and for the resolution of the U(1) problem in QCD. Gauge anomalies must cancel for consistency. In the Standard Model they cancel between quarks and leptons.

The cancellation is a constraint on the particle content. It is satisfied by the observed fermions. Gravitational anomalies impose further constraints. Anomalies are not defects. They are calculable quantum effects that have observable consequences. Their cancellation or non-cancellation determines which theories are consistent.

title: Instantons
paras: Instantons are classical solutions of the Euclidean field equations. They describe tunnelling between topologically distinct vacua. In QCD they contribute to the mass of the eta-prime and to the violation of U(1) axial symmetry. Their density is suppressed at high temperature. The suppression is observed in the restoration of the symmetry above the deconfinement transition.

In the electroweak theory instantons violate baryon and lepton number. The rate is negligible at zero temperature. It becomes unsuppressed above the electroweak scale. The process is the basis of electroweak baryogenesis and of leptogenesis scenarios that rely on sphalerons. Instantons are non-perturbative. They are not captured by Feynman diagrams. They are required for a complete description of the vacuum structure.

title: The Theta Term and the Strong CP Problem
paras: The QCD Lagrangian admits a term proportional to the topological charge. The coefficient is an angle \( \theta \). The term violates CP. Experimental limits on the neutron electric dipole moment require \( \theta \) to be smaller than \( 10^{-10} \). No symmetry of the Standard Model sets \( \theta \) to zero. The smallness is the strong CP problem.

The Peccei–Quinn mechanism promotes \( \theta \) to a dynamical field. The field relaxes to zero. Its excitation is the axion. The axion is a candidate for dark matter. Laboratory and astrophysical searches constrain its mass and coupling. No detection has been confirmed. The mechanism solves the strong CP problem if the axion exists. The existence is not yet established.

title: Axions
paras: Axions are hypothetical particles that solve the strong CP problem. They are light, weakly interacting, and can constitute the dark matter. The mass is inversely proportional to the decay constant. Astrophysical bounds require the decay constant to be large, so the mass is small—microelectronvolts or below for the dark-matter window.

Searches use resonant cavities in magnetic fields, nuclear magnetic resonance, and broadband techniques. The cavity experiments scan the mass range by tuning the frequency. No signal has been found in the ranges examined. The remaining parameter space is large. A detection would solve both the strong CP problem and the dark-matter problem. The absence of a detection so far constrains but does not exclude the particle.

title: Sterile Neutrinos
paras: Sterile neutrinos are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group. They interact only through mixing with the active neutrinos or through gravity. They are required in the seesaw mechanism. Their masses can range from sub-electronvolt to the grand-unification scale. Light sterile neutrinos have been invoked to explain anomalies in short-baseline oscillation experiments. The anomalies are not confirmed by all experiments.

Cosmological bounds limit the contribution of light sterile neutrinos to the energy density in the early universe. The bounds are in tension with the parameter space preferred by some anomalies. Heavy sterile neutrinos are constrained by the non-observation of their decay products and by the success of Big Bang nucleosynthesis. The particles remain hypothetical. They are a minimal extension that can generate neutrino masses.

title: Leptogenesis
paras: Leptogenesis generates the baryon asymmetry from a lepton asymmetry. Heavy right-handed neutrinos decay out of equilibrium. The decays violate CP. The resulting lepton asymmetry is partially converted into a baryon asymmetry by electroweak sphalerons. The mechanism operates naturally within the seesaw framework.

The required right-handed neutrino masses lie above \( 10^9 \) GeV in the simplest versions. Lower scales are possible with resonant enhancement or with additional fields. The mechanism links the baryon asymmetry to the origin of neutrino masses. It has not been experimentally confirmed. It remains the most economical explanation that connects two otherwise separate facts—the smallness of neutrino masses and the existence of the baryon asymmetry.

title: Electroweak Baryogenesis
paras: Electroweak baryogenesis generates the baryon asymmetry during the electroweak phase transition. A strongly first-order transition provides the departure from equilibrium. CP violation in the bubble walls generates a chiral asymmetry. Sphalerons convert it into a baryon asymmetry outside the bubbles. Inside the bubbles the sphalerons are suppressed and the asymmetry is frozen.

The Standard Model transition is a crossover. It is not first-order. Extensions that strengthen the transition—additional scalars, supersymmetry—are required. Those extensions are constrained by the Higgs mass and by the non-observation of new particles. The mechanism is testable. It predicts electric dipole moments and modifications of the Higgs potential. Neither has been observed at the required level. The scenario remains possible in limited regions of parameter space.

title: The Hierarchy Problem
paras: The hierarchy problem is the sensitivity of the Higgs mass to ultraviolet physics. Quadratic divergences require fine-tuning if the cutoff lies far above the electroweak scale. The fine-tuning is of order \( (v/\Lambda)^2 \). For a Planck-scale cutoff it is one part in \( 10^{32} \). No symmetry of the Standard Model protects the mass.

Supersymmetry cancels the quadratic divergences. Composite Higgs models replace the elementary scalar with a bound state. Extra dimensions lower the cutoff. None of these solutions has been confirmed. The absence of superpartners below a TeV increases the residual tuning. The problem is conceptual. It is not a contradiction with data. It is a reason to expect new physics near the electroweak scale. That expectation has not yet been fulfilled.

title: Naturalness
paras: Naturalness is the expectation that dimensionless parameters of order one are typical and that large hierarchies require explanation. The expectation is aesthetic and historical. It has been successful in some cases—the charm quark was predicted by the absence of flavour-changing neutral currents. It has failed in others—the cosmological constant is unnaturally small.

The failure does not invalidate the criterion. It shows that the criterion is not infallible. Anthropic selection or environmental scanning can produce apparently unnatural values. The criterion remains a guide for model building. It is not a theorem. Its continued use is justified by its past successes and tempered by its known failures.

title: Supersymmetry
paras: Supersymmetry relates bosons and fermions. Each particle has a superpartner whose spin differs by one-half. The symmetry cancels quadratic divergences and unifies the gauge couplings at a high scale. It supplies a dark-matter candidate if R-parity is conserved. The lightest superpartner is stable.

No superpartners have been observed. Limits from colliders exceed a TeV for many coloured states. The limits increase the residual fine-tuning. The symmetry may be broken at a higher scale. It may be absent. The motivations—hierarchy, unification, dark matter—remain. The experimental support is absent. The theory is a well-motivated extension that has not been confirmed.

title: Extra Dimensions
paras: Extra spatial dimensions can be compactified on a small manifold. The compactification radius determines the mass scale of the Kaluza–Klein excitations. If the radius is large enough the excitations may be accessible at colliders. No such excitations have been observed. Limits on the radius depend on the number of extra dimensions and on the energy.

Warped extra dimensions can generate hierarchies exponentially. The Randall–Sundrum model places the Higgs on a brane where the warp factor suppresses its mass. The model predicts Kaluza–Klein gravitons. They have not been seen. Extra dimensions remain a possible ultraviolet completion. They are constrained by precision tests and by the non-observation of new particles. The constraints do not exclude all realisations.

title: String Compactifications
paras: String theory requires additional dimensions. Compactification on a Calabi–Yau manifold preserves supersymmetry in the low-energy theory. Fluxes and branes stabilise the moduli. The number of distinct compactifications is large—the landscape. Each yields a different four-dimensional effective theory. The vast majority do not resemble the Standard Model.

No principle selects the compactification that reproduces the observed particle content and couplings. Anthropic selection among those that permit observers is one proposal. It is not predictive beyond the requirement of habitability. The compactifications demonstrate that string theory can produce four-dimensional physics. They do not yet demonstrate that it produces our physics. The gap is the absence of a selection mechanism.

title: The Swampland
paras: The swampland is the set of effective field theories that cannot be consistently coupled to quantum gravity. Swampland conjectures propose criteria that separate the landscape from the swampland. One conjecture states that the scalar potential must satisfy a lower bound on its gradient. Another states that towers of light states appear when a scalar field traverses a large distance in field space.

The conjectures are motivated by examples in string theory. They are not proven. If true, they constrain inflation and the cosmological constant. Some versions are in tension with the observed dark energy. The conjectures illustrate an attempt to extract general lessons from string theory without a complete non-perturbative definition. Their status is provisional.

title: Holography and Entanglement
paras: The Ryu–Takayanagi formula equates the entanglement entropy of a boundary region with the area of a bulk minimal surface. The formula has been verified in many examples. It suggests that spacetime geometry is encoded in the entanglement structure of the boundary theory. The suggestion is precise in anti-de Sitter space. Its extension to other asymptotics is incomplete.

Entanglement wedge reconstruction shows that bulk operators inside the wedge can be represented as boundary operators. The reconstruction is state-dependent for operators behind horizons. The dependence is consistent with the island calculations of black-hole evaporation. Holography therefore supplies both a definition of quantum gravity in certain spacetimes and a concrete realisation of the idea that geometry emerges from entanglement.

title: The Information Paradox in AdS/CFT
paras: In AdS/CFT the formation and evaporation of a black hole is dual to the unitary evolution of a thermal state in the boundary theory. Unitarity is therefore guaranteed. The paradox becomes the question of how the bulk calculation reproduces the unitary result. The island formula and the replica wormhole provide the bulk mechanism. They modify the entropy calculation after the Page time.

The resolution is explicit in low-dimensional models and in certain supersymmetric theories. Its extension to higher-dimensional, asymptotically flat black holes is not complete. The AdS/CFT example demonstrates that a unitary resolution is possible within a consistent theory of quantum gravity. It does not yet supply the resolution for the black holes that form in our universe.

title: Firewalls
paras: The firewall argument states that unitarity, the equivalence principle and effective field theory outside the horizon cannot all be maintained for an old black hole. The monogamy of entanglement is the obstruction. One of the three assumptions must fail. A firewall is a high-energy barrier at the horizon that preserves unitarity at the cost of the equivalence principle.

The argument has not been resolved. Island calculations suggest that the interior is not independent of the exterior radiation after the Page time. The suggestion softens the conflict. It does not eliminate it for all observers. The firewall remains a possible outcome. It is not required by present calculations. The tension between unitarity and smoothness is real. Its resolution is model-dependent.

title: The Page Curve in Detail
paras: The Page curve is the entanglement entropy of the radiation as a function of time. For a unitary evaporation it rises until the Page time and then falls to zero. The rise is the accumulation of entanglement. The fall is the release of that entanglement in correlations. A thermal spectrum produces only the rise. The fall requires non-thermal correlations.

Island calculations reproduce the fall. The quantum extremal surface moves behind the horizon after the Page time. The generalised entropy decreases. The calculation is semi-classical. It captures the leading entanglement. It does not construct the microscopic operators that purify the radiation. The existence of the curve in the calculation is evidence that a unitary resolution is compatible with semi-classical gravity. The microscopic realisation remains open.

title: Replica Wormholes
paras: Replica wormholes are saddle points of the gravitational path integral that compute the entanglement entropy. They connect the replicas of the radiation through the black-hole interior. Their contribution dominates after the Page time. The dominance produces the turnover of the Page curve. The wormholes are not traversable. They are a calculational device.

The same saddles appear in the calculation of the purity and of higher Rényi entropies. They are required for consistency with unitarity. Their existence in the path integral is a consequence of the Euclidean gravitational action. It does not imply that an observer can travel through them. The wormholes resolve the entropy calculation. They do not by themselves resolve the experience of the infalling observer.

title: The Island Formula
paras: The island formula computes the entanglement entropy of the radiation as the minimum of the generalised entropy of a region that includes an island inside the black hole. The formula is \[ S = \min \left( \frac{\mathrm{Area}(\partial I)}{4G_N} + S_{\mathrm{matter}}(R \cup I) \right). \] The minimum is taken over islands \( I \). After the Page time the minimum includes a non-empty island. The formula reproduces the Page curve.

It has been derived from the replica trick in gravitational path integrals. It applies to evaporating black holes in anti-de Sitter space and in certain flat-space models. Its validity for realistic astrophysical black holes is assumed but not proven. The formula is the sharpest present statement of how information escapes. It remains a semi-classical expression.

title: Quantum Extremal Surfaces
paras: A quantum extremal surface is a surface that extremises the generalised entropy. It reduces to the ordinary Ryu–Takayanagi surface when the bulk entropy is negligible. When the bulk entropy is large the surface moves. In the island calculation the quantum extremal surface lies inside the horizon after the Page time. Its area plus the bulk entropy of the island and the radiation gives the Page curve.

The surface is a generalisation of the classical extremal surface. It incorporates the leading quantum correction. Higher-order corrections exist. They are small in the semi-classical limit. The concept unifies the classical area term with the bulk entanglement. It is the geometric object that appears in the island formula and in the derivation of the Page curve.

title: The Black-Hole Interior
paras: The interior of a black hole is the region behind the event horizon. In classical general relativity it is causally disconnected from the exterior. In the quantum theory the disconnection is not absolute. The island calculations assign part of the interior to the entanglement wedge of the exterior radiation after the Page time. The assignment is state-dependent.

An infalling observer encounters a smooth geometry in the semi-classical approximation. The approximation fails near the singularity and, possibly, at the horizon of an old black hole. The failure at the horizon is the firewall question. No consensus exists. The interior is both a region of classical spacetime and a quantum system whose degrees of freedom are shared with the exterior. The sharing is the content of the island formula. Its implications for the experience of the infalling observer remain under debate.

title: The Measurement Problem
paras: The measurement problem is the question of how a definite outcome emerges from a quantum superposition. The Schrödinger equation is linear and deterministic. It does not by itself select one outcome. The Born rule gives probabilities. It does not describe the occurrence of a single result. Collapse postulates add the selection by hand. They are not derived from the unitary dynamics.

Decoherence explains the suppression of interference. It does not explain the occurrence of one outcome rather than another. Many-worlds interpretations deny that a selection occurs. Bohmian mechanics adds particle positions. Objective-collapse models modify the equation. None is established. The problem is the gap between the unitary formalism and the definite events of experience. The gap remains open.

title: Decoherence in Detail
paras: Decoherence is the loss of phase coherence between components of a superposition through interaction with an environment. The reduced density matrix of the system becomes diagonal in a preferred basis. Interference terms vanish. The preferred basis is selected by the interaction Hamiltonian. For macroscopic objects the basis is approximately the position basis.

The process is rapid for macroscopic superpositions. It is slow for carefully isolated microscopic systems. Decoherence accounts for the classical appearance of everyday objects. It does not solve the measurement problem. The diagonal density matrix is an improper mixture. It does not correspond to a definite outcome. The process is necessary for classicality. It is not sufficient for the emergence of single events.

title: Many-Worlds Interpretation
paras: The many-worlds interpretation asserts that the universal wave function evolves unitarily at all times. Apparent collapse is the branching of the wave function into non-interfering components. Each component corresponds to a definite outcome. All outcomes occur. Observers are themselves branched.

The interpretation avoids additional postulates. It must explain the origin of probabilities. Derivations from decision theory or from self-locating uncertainty have been proposed. They are not universally accepted. The interpretation is consistent. It is not experimentally distinguishable from interpretations that add collapse, provided the collapse is irreversible and the branches do not interfere. The ontological cost is the reality of the unobserved branches.

title: Bohmian Mechanics
paras: Bohmian mechanics supplements the wave function with particle positions. The positions evolve according to a guidance equation determined by the wave function. The wave function itself evolves by the Schrödinger equation. The particles have definite positions at all times. The apparent randomness arises from ignorance of the initial positions.

The theory reproduces the Born-rule statistics for a particular distribution of initial positions. The distribution is preserved by the dynamics. The theory is deterministic and non-local. The non-locality is required by Bell’s theorem. It does not permit signalling. The theory is empirically equivalent to standard quantum mechanics. Its advantage is ontological clarity. Its cost is the addition of unobservable trajectories and the explicit non-locality.

title: Objective Collapse Models
paras: Objective collapse models modify the Schrödinger equation so that superpositions of macroscopically distinct states decay spontaneously. The collapse is a physical process. It occurs with a rate that increases with the number of particles. Microscopic systems are essentially unaffected. Macroscopic superpositions collapse rapidly.

The models predict deviations from standard quantum mechanics. The deviations are small. They are constrained by matter-wave interferometry and by the absence of anomalous heating. No deviation has been observed. The models solve the measurement problem by altering the dynamics. They introduce new parameters. The parameters are bounded but not excluded. The models remain possible extensions.

title: Quantum Darwinism
paras: Quantum Darwinism proposes that the classical world emerges through the redundant encoding of information in the environment. Pointer states are those that survive decoherence and proliferate their information. Observers who access fragments of the environment obtain the same information. The redundancy defines objectivity.

The proposal accounts for the preferred basis and for the agreement among observers. It does not select a single outcome. All pointer states are encoded. The appearance of a single outcome still requires an interpretation of the branching or an additional postulate. The framework is consistent with decoherence. It extends it by emphasising redundancy. It remains an account of classicality, not a solution to the measurement problem.

title: Consistent Histories
paras: The consistent-histories approach assigns probabilities to sets of histories that satisfy a consistency condition. The condition ensures that the probabilities obey the classical sum rules. Inconsistent sets do not receive probabilities. The approach avoids explicit collapse. It requires the selection of a consistent set. The selection is not given by the formalism.

Different consistent sets can be incompatible. The approach does not privilege one. It therefore does not explain why one set of events is experienced. It supplies a framework in which classical reasoning can be applied to quantum systems. The framework is mathematically precise. The physical interpretation of the multiplicity of sets remains open.

title: Relational Quantum Mechanics
paras: Relational quantum mechanics asserts that the quantum state of a system is relative to another system. There is no absolute state. Events are interactions. The state is the information that one system has about another. The approach dissolves the measurement problem by denying the existence of an observer-independent state.

The approach is consistent with the predictions of quantum mechanics. It requires care in the treatment of sequences of measurements. It does not add dynamical postulates. Its cost is the abandonment of an absolute quantum state. The cost is accepted by its proponents as the price of consistency. The approach remains a minority interpretation.

title: Quantum Bayesianism
paras: Quantum Bayesianism interprets the quantum state as an agent’s information or degrees of belief. The state is not a property of the system. It is a property of the agent. Measurement updates the agent’s beliefs. The approach avoids ontological questions about collapse. It relocates the state to the agent.

The approach reproduces the operational predictions. It must explain why agents who communicate agree. The explanation relies on the common information acquired through interaction. The approach is operationally clear. Its metaphysical claim—that the state is not ontic—is disputed. The dispute does not affect the calculations. It affects the interpretation of what the calculations describe.

title: The Quantum-to-Classical Transition
paras: The quantum-to-classical transition is the emergence of classical behaviour from quantum mechanics. Decoherence suppresses interference. The remaining diagonal density matrix can be interpreted as a classical mixture for practical purposes. The interpretation is adequate for prediction. It is incomplete for ontology.

The transition is continuous. Mesoscopic systems display partial coherence. The degree of classicality increases with the separation of the components and with the strength of the environmental interaction. No sharp boundary exists. The transition is well-described by decoherence for all practical purposes. The residual conceptual questions are those of the measurement problem. They are not resolved by the practical success.

title: Bell’s Theorem in Detail
paras: Bell’s theorem states that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce the predictions of quantum mechanics. The CHSH inequality bounds the correlations permitted by local realism. Quantum mechanics predicts a violation up to \( 2\sqrt{2} \). Experiments have measured violations close to the quantum bound. The experiments have closed the detection, locality and freedom-of-choice loopholes.

The theorem does not require non-local signalling. It requires that the outcomes are not determined by local variables in the manner assumed by the inequality. The experimental violations confirm the quantum predictions. They exclude local realistic completions of the sort Bell considered. They do not exclude all conceivable completions. They exclude those that satisfy the assumptions of the theorem.

title: The Free Will Theorem
paras: The free will theorem of Conway and Kochen states that if experimenters have freedom in the choice of measurement settings, then the responses of entangled particles are not determined by prior information. The theorem assumes the quantum predictions and a locality condition. It concludes that the particles’ responses are not functions of the past.

The theorem is a variant of Bell’s theorem. It emphasises the freedom of the experimenter. The freedom is the assumption that the settings are not correlated with the hidden variables. The assumption is necessary for the derivation. It is not proven. The theorem sharpens the conflict between determinism, locality and the quantum predictions. It does not resolve it.

title: Leggett–Garg Inequalities
paras: Leggett–Garg inequalities bound the correlations of measurements performed on a single system at different times. They assume macroscopic realism and non-invasive measurability. Quantum mechanics violates the inequalities. The violations have been observed in superconducting qubits, photons and other systems.

The inequalities test the applicability of classical realism to macroscopic objects. Their violation shows that the systems do not possess pre-existing values that are merely revealed by measurement. The tests are complementary to Bell tests. They probe temporal rather than spatial correlations. The violations confirm the quantum predictions for the systems examined. They do not yet extend to everyday macroscopic objects.

title: Contextuality
paras: Contextuality is the dependence of measurement outcomes on the set of compatible measurements performed together. The Kochen–Specker theorem shows that no non-contextual hidden-variable theory can reproduce the predictions of quantum mechanics in Hilbert spaces of dimension greater than two. The theorem is state-independent.

Contextuality is a feature of the quantum formalism. It has been demonstrated in experiments with photons, neutrons and ions. It is a resource for quantum computation. Certain computational advantages require contextuality. The phenomenon is distinct from non-locality. It appears in single systems. It is a fundamental obstruction to classical simulations of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Steering
paras: Quantum steering is the ability of one party to influence the state of a distant party by choice of measurement. It is intermediate between entanglement and Bell non-locality. Not all entangled states are steerable. All Bell-nonlocal states are steerable. Steering can be verified with one trusted and one untrusted party.

The phenomenon has been demonstrated experimentally. It is a resource for one-sided device-independent cryptography. The hierarchy—entanglement, steering, Bell non-locality—organises the strengths of quantum correlation. Each level excludes a larger set of classical models. Steering is the intermediate level. It is both theoretically sharp and experimentally accessible.

title: Device-Independent Quantum Information
paras: Device-independent protocols rely only on the observed correlations. They do not require characterisation of the devices. Security is certified by the violation of a Bell inequality. The certification is independent of the internal workings of the apparatus. Quantum key distribution and random-number generation have been implemented in the device-independent setting.

The implementations require high-efficiency detection and space-like separation. Both have been achieved. The rates are low. The principle is established. Practical deployment awaits higher rates and longer distances. The approach eliminates side-channel attacks that exploit imperfect device characterisation. It replaces them with the requirement of a loophole-free Bell violation.

title: Quantum Key Distribution
paras: Quantum key distribution allows two parties to generate a shared secret key. Security rests on the no-cloning theorem and on the disturbance caused by measurement. The BB84 protocol uses four polarisation states. The E91 protocol uses entangled pairs and Bell violation. Both have been implemented over optical fibre and free space.

The secret-key rate decreases with distance because of loss and noise. Quantum repeaters are required for global distances. Prototype repeaters exist. They are not yet practical. The security proofs assume ideal devices or are device-independent. Real devices introduce side channels. Countermeasures exist. The protocols are information-theoretically secure under the stated assumptions. The assumptions must be enforced in practice.

title: Quantum Teleportation
paras: Quantum teleportation transfers an unknown quantum state from one system to another using a shared entangled pair and classical communication. The sender performs a joint measurement. The receiver applies a correction conditioned on the classical result. The state is destroyed at the sender and recreated at the receiver. No information is transmitted faster than light.

Teleportation has been demonstrated with photons, atoms, ions and superconducting circuits. It is a primitive for quantum networks and for measurement-based computation. The fidelity is limited by the quality of the entanglement and by the accuracy of the operations. High-fidelity teleportation over laboratory distances is routine. Extension to long distances requires quantum repeaters. The protocol is both a fundamental demonstration and a practical tool.

title: Quantum Networks
paras: A quantum network distributes entanglement and transmits quantum states among multiple nodes. The nodes are quantum processors or memories. The links are photonic channels. Quantum repeaters extend the range by entanglement swapping and purification. The network enables distributed quantum computation, blind quantum computation and long-distance key distribution.

Prototype networks with a few nodes exist. They demonstrate entanglement distribution and teleportation. Scaling to many nodes requires memories with long coherence times, high-efficiency interfaces, and error correction. The requirements are engineering challenges. The architectural principles are established. The network is the quantum analogue of the classical internet. It does not yet exist at comparable scale.

title: Blind Quantum Computation
paras: Blind quantum computation allows a client to delegate a computation to a server without revealing the input, the output or the algorithm. The client prepares single qubits and sends them to the server. The server entangles them and measures according to instructions. The instructions are chosen so that the server learns nothing about the computation. The client obtains the result.

The protocol has been demonstrated with photonic systems. Security rests on the no-signalling principle and on the client’s ability to prepare states from a restricted set. The protocol enables private computation on a remote quantum computer. It does not require the client to possess a universal quantum computer. The client needs only to prepare and measure single qubits. The capability is a distinctive feature of quantum networks.

title: Topological Quantum Computation
paras: Topological quantum computation encodes information in non-Abelian anyons. The information is stored in the fusion space. Gates are implemented by braiding. The braiding is topological. It is insensitive to local perturbations. The protection is passive. Error correction is still required for non-topological operations and for leakage.

Ising anyons are realised in the fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor 5/2 and in certain superconducting systems. They are not universal. Additional non-topological gates are needed. Fibonacci anyons are universal. They have not been realised. The approach offers high thresholds in principle. The experimental realisation of non-Abelian anyons with the required properties remains incomplete. The theoretical framework is mature.

title: Measurement-Based Quantum Computation
paras: Measurement-based quantum computation performs the computation by a sequence of single-qubit measurements on a pre-entangled resource state. The resource is a cluster state or a graph state. The measurements are adaptive. The basis of each measurement depends on previous outcomes. The computation is equivalent to the circuit model.

The approach separates the creation of entanglement from the computation. The entanglement can be prepared offline. The computation itself consists of measurements. The separation is advantageous for photonic implementations. Photon loss remains the principal error. Error correction is possible. The model is universal. It has been demonstrated on small scales. Scaling requires high-fidelity resource states and feed-forward.

title: Adiabatic Quantum Computation
paras: Adiabatic quantum computation encodes the solution of a problem in the ground state of a final Hamiltonian. The system is prepared in the ground state of an initial Hamiltonian and evolved slowly to the final Hamiltonian. The adiabatic theorem guarantees that the system remains in the ground state if the evolution is slow enough. The runtime scales with the inverse square of the minimum gap.

The model is universal. It is equivalent to the circuit model. Practical implementations are limited by the gap and by thermal excitations. Quantum annealing is a related heuristic. It does not guarantee the ground state. Both approaches are studied for optimisation problems. Speed-ups over classical algorithms are not guaranteed for all instances. They are possible for some.

title: Quantum Annealing
paras: Quantum annealing is a heuristic method for finding the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian. A transverse field is applied and slowly reduced. Tunnelling allows the system to escape local minima. The method does not guarantee the optimal solution. It can outperform simulated annealing on some instances. It can underperform on others.

Commercial devices implement quantum annealing with thousands of qubits. The qubits are noisy. The connectivity is limited. Benchmarking against classical algorithms is ongoing. Advantages have been claimed for specific problem classes. The claims are contested. The devices are useful for studying quantum dynamics. Their advantage for practical optimisation remains unproven.

title: Variational Quantum Algorithms
paras: Variational quantum algorithms use a parameterised quantum circuit and a classical optimiser. The circuit prepares a trial state. The classical optimiser adjusts the parameters to minimise a cost function. The approach is hybrid. It is suitable for noisy intermediate-scale devices. The quantum approximate optimisation algorithm and the variational quantum eigensolver are examples.

The algorithms do not require fault tolerance. Their performance is limited by noise and by the difficulty of the classical optimisation. Barren plateaus—regions of exponentially small gradients—impede training for some circuits. Mitigation strategies exist. The algorithms are a practical approach for present hardware. Their asymptotic advantage is not established.

title: Substantial Expansion: The Standard Model
paras: The Standard Model is a renormalisable quantum field theory based on the gauge group \( SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \). It contains three generations of quarks and leptons, a single Higgs doublet, and the gauge bosons. The Lagrangian is fixed once the representations and the couplings are specified. Nineteen parameters (or more if neutrinos are included) remain free. They are measured, not predicted.

Precision tests confirm the model to high accuracy. The electron anomalous magnetic moment agrees with theory to more than ten figures. The W and Z masses, the weak mixing angle and the Higgs mass match the predictions after radiative corrections. Neutrino masses require an extension. Dark matter, the baryon asymmetry and the cosmological constant lie outside the model. The theory is the most successful description of the non-gravitational interactions. Its incompleteness is quantitative and observational. No contradiction with existing data has been established. No complete ultraviolet completion is known.

title: Substantial Expansion: General Relativity
paras: General relativity identifies gravity with the curvature of spacetime. The Einstein equation relates the curvature to the stress-energy tensor. The equation is non-linear. Solutions include the Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes, the Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker cosmologies, and gravitational waves. The theory has passed every experimental test from laboratory scales to cosmological scales.

The equivalence principle, gravitational redshift, light deflection, the Shapiro delay, frame-dragging and the binary-pulsar decay all agree with the predictions. Gravitational-wave observations match the waveforms computed from numerical relativity. The theory fails at singularities and is incompatible with quantum mechanics in its present form. Quantum corrections are expected near the Planck scale. No observational evidence of those corrections exists. The classical theory remains the standard description of gravity wherever curvature is not extreme.

title: Substantial Expansion: Quantum Field Theory
paras: Quantum field theory is the framework that combines quantum mechanics with special relativity. Particles are excitations of fields. Interactions are local. The S-matrix is computed perturbatively by Feynman diagrams or non-perturbatively by lattice methods or by other techniques. Renormalisation renders the predictions finite in renormalisable theories.

The framework encompasses the Standard Model, effective theories of the strong interaction, and condensed-matter systems. It predicts the existence of antiparticles, the spin-statistics connection, and the CPT theorem. It does not include gravity in a consistent way. Attempts to quantise gravity perturbatively fail because the theory is non-renormalisable. Non-perturbative approaches—string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety—remain incomplete. Quantum field theory is nevertheless the language in which the most precise predictions in physics are formulated.

title: Substantial Expansion: Cosmology
paras: The standard cosmological model describes a universe that expanded from a hot, dense state. The model is based on general relativity and on the Standard Model of particle physics, supplemented by cold dark matter and a cosmological constant. It accounts for the expansion, the microwave background, the abundances of the light elements, and the large-scale distribution of galaxies.

Six parameters suffice to fit the microwave-background data. The same parameters predict the baryon acoustic scale and the growth of structure. The predictions agree with observations. Tensions exist. The Hubble constant inferred locally differs from the value inferred from the microwave background. The amplitude of matter fluctuations shows milder discrepancies. The tensions may indicate new physics or unrecognised systematics. The model remains the standard. Its domain of validity is large. Its completeness is not established.

title: Substantial Expansion: Evolution
paras: Evolution by natural selection is the change in allele frequencies caused by differential reproductive success. Variation is generated by mutation and recombination. Selection, drift and migration alter the frequencies. The process produces adaptation and, given reproductive isolation, speciation. The theory is supported by the fossil record, by comparative anatomy, by biogeography, and by molecular sequences.

The modern synthesis integrates Mendelian genetics with natural selection. Subsequent additions include neutral theory, kin selection, and the recognition of horizontal gene transfer and epigenetic inheritance. None replaces the core. The core accounts for the fit between organisms and their environments and for the hierarchical pattern of similarity. The theory is as well-established as any in science. Open questions concern the relative importance of the various mechanisms and the detailed history of particular lineages. The questions are empirical. They do not threaten the framework.

title: The Moment the Rules Changed
paras: In 1905 a patent clerk in Bern published three papers. One showed that light comes in packets. One showed that atoms are real. One showed that time and space are not what they seem. None of the papers was long. None required a large laboratory. Together they dismantled the classical picture of the world.

The clerk was not trying to be revolutionary. He was trying to remove inconsistencies. The inconsistencies would not go. Maxwell’s equations refused to tolerate a preferred frame. The photoelectric effect refused to tolerate continuous energy. Brownian motion refused to tolerate a continuum without atoms. The resolutions were simple once stated. They were not simple to accept. Acceptance took years. The years did not restore the old rules. The old rules were gone.

The episode is the clearest modern example of a quiet calculation overturning an entire ontology. It has not been the last. It remains the standard against which later revolutions are measured. Most of them have been louder. None has been cleaner.

title: What the Sky Is Doing While You Read This
paras: While you read this sentence the Earth has moved roughly 30 kilometres in its orbit. The Solar System has moved roughly 220 kilometres around the Galactic centre. The Galaxy has moved several hundred kilometres relative to the cosmic microwave background. None of these motions is felt. All of them are real.

The photons striking your retina left their sources long ago. Some left the Sun eight minutes ago. Some left distant galaxies when the Earth was young. A few, if you are looking at the microwave background, left when the universe was 380 000 years old. They have been travelling ever since. They will continue after you stop reading.

The calculations that describe these motions and these journeys are the same calculations that describe the fall of an apple and the swing of a pendulum. The scales differ. The laws do not. The recognition is ordinary once it is made. It is still capable of producing a slight shift in the way the next sentence is read.

title: The Experiment That Should Not Have Worked
paras: In 1887 Michelson and Morley measured the speed of light in two perpendicular directions. They expected a difference. The Earth is moving. Light should take longer in the direction of motion. The difference was not there. The experiment was repeated. The difference was still not there.

The null result eliminated the luminiferous aether. It did not immediately suggest the correct replacement. Lorentz and Fitzgerald proposed length contraction as a patch. Einstein proposed that the speed of light is the same in every inertial frame and that simultaneity is relative. The proposal was not a patch. It was a replacement. The replacement survived every subsequent test.

The experiment is still cited because it is simple, decisive, and historically pivotal. Modern versions reach precisions of parts in \( 10^{17} \). The null result remains. The aether has not returned. The lesson is that a sufficiently clean null result can remove an entire theoretical structure. The structure does not always notice at once.

title: A Number That Should Not Be Small
paras: The cosmological constant is small. It is not zero. Quantum field theory expects it to be enormous. The discrepancy is 50 to 120 orders of magnitude, depending on the cutoff. No symmetry cancels it. No dynamical mechanism is known to relax it. The value is measured. The measurement is precise. The explanation is absent.

The smallness permits galaxies, stars and observers. A larger value would have prevented structure formation. The observation has led to anthropic arguments. The arguments may be correct. They are not explanatory in the ordinary sense. They do not derive the value from a dynamical principle. They derive the fact that observers find a small value from the fact that observers exist.

The constant is therefore both the dominant component of the present universe and the least understood. Its smallness is the sharpest quantitative failure of present theory. The failure is not hidden. It is written in the expansion rate of the universe and in the existence of the reader.

title: The Protein That Should Not Fold
paras: A protein is a chain of amino acids. The chain folds into a specific three-dimensional structure in milliseconds to seconds. The number of possible conformations is astronomical. A random search would take longer than the age of the universe. The chain nevertheless finds the native structure reliably. The discrepancy is Levinthal’s paradox.

The resolution is that the search is not random. The energy landscape is funnelled. Local interactions guide the chain toward the native state. Folding intermediates and chaperones assist. Misfolding occurs. It is the exception. The exception produces disease. The rule produces function.

The process is a demonstration that a high-dimensional search can be efficient when the landscape is structured. The structure is encoded in the sequence. The sequence is encoded in the genome. The genome is the product of selection. The selection has produced chains that fold. The chains that do not fold are not here. The reader is composed of those that do.

title: The Collision That Made the Moon
paras: Four and a half billion years ago a body the size of Mars struck the Earth. The impact melted both. Debris was thrown into orbit. Most of the iron had already sunk into the Earth’s core, so the debris was rocky. It gathered into the Moon. The whole event lasted hours. The consequences are still here.

The Moon stabilises the Earth’s obliquity. Without it the tilt would wander chaotically. Seasons would be unpredictable. The impact also set the length of the day and the distance to the Moon. Both have changed since. The day has lengthened. The Moon has receded. The recession is measured. It is 3.8 centimetres per year. The measurement is a laser beam bounced off a mirror left by astronauts. The mirror is still there. The beam still returns.

The collision is the reason there is a large moon, a stable climate, and a mirror on the lunar surface. It is also the reason the Earth–Moon system carries a particular angular momentum. The angular momentum is a fossil of the impact. It has not been erased.

title: The Signal That Travelled for a Billion Years
paras: In 2015 a gravitational-wave detector in Louisiana twitched. A second detector in Washington twitched 7 milliseconds later. The twitches matched the waveform of two black holes spiralling together and merging. The black holes were 1.3 billion light-years away. The signal had been travelling since before animals existed. It arrived on a September morning.

The detectors had been built to measure a change in length of one part in \( 10^{21} \). That is a fraction of the diameter of a proton across a 4-kilometre arm. The change was detected. The waveform matched the prediction of general relativity to high precision. No other known process produces that waveform. The black holes merged. The waves crossed the universe. The mirrors moved. The movement was recorded.

The event was the first direct detection of gravitational waves and the first observation of a binary black-hole merger. It was also a demonstration that a prediction made a century earlier, about a distortion of spacetime too small to imagine, could be turned into a recorded trace. The trace is now routine. It was not routine that morning.

title: The Bacterium That Changed the Air
paras: Two and a half billion years ago cyanobacteria began to produce oxygen as a waste product. The oxygen was absorbed by iron and by reduced gases. When those sinks were full, the oxygen accumulated. The atmosphere changed. The change killed most of the anaerobic organisms then alive. It also made aerobic respiration possible. Aerobic respiration yields far more energy per glucose molecule. The energy made larger bodies possible.

The event is recorded in the rocks. Banded-iron formations stop. Red beds appear. The carbon isotopes shift. The shift is permanent. Every breath taken since has depended on it. The cyanobacteria did not plan the change. They excreted a gas. The gas altered the planet. The alteration permitted the reader. The reader is still dependent on the descendants of those bacteria, or on the chloroplasts that were once those bacteria. The dependence is total. It is not usually noticed.

title: The Inequality That Cannot Be Satisfied
paras: In 1964 John Bell wrote an inequality that any local hidden-variable theory must obey. Quantum mechanics predicts that the inequality can be violated. The prediction was tested. It was violated. The violation has been confirmed with photons, atoms, ions and superconducting circuits. The loopholes have been closed. The inequality is not satisfied.

The result does not permit faster-than-light signalling. It does eliminate the possibility that the outcomes were determined in advance by local variables. The correlations are stronger than any local mechanism can produce. The experiments are now undergraduate demonstrations. They were not always so. The first tests were delicate. The latest are conclusive. Nature does not obey the inequality. The inequality is what local realism requires. Local realism is therefore false. The falsity is not subtle. It is measured.

title: The Map That Contains Itself
paras: A cell contains a genome. The genome contains the instructions for building the cell, including the machinery that reads the genome. The map contains the instructions for building the map-reader. The arrangement is ordinary. It is also the reason life can persist. Without the map the machinery cannot be rebuilt. Without the machinery the map cannot be read. Both are required. Both are copied.

The copying is imperfect. The imperfections are mutations. Most are harmful or neutral. A few are beneficial. The beneficial ones spread. The spread is evolution. The evolution has produced organisms that contain maps of themselves accurate enough to build the next generation. The accuracy is high. It is not perfect. The imperfection is the source of all subsequent change. The change includes the reader. The reader is still carrying a slightly imperfect copy of the map.

title: A Note on Progress
paras: Progress in science is the replacement of a vague idea by a precise one, followed by the discovery that the precise idea is wrong in a smaller way. The smaller wrongness is an improvement. It is not a reason for celebration. It is a reason to continue.

The pattern is reliable. It is also slow. The slowness is not a defect of the method. It is a consequence of the requirement that the new idea must survive contact with observation. Contact with observation is frequently inconvenient. The inconvenience is the point. Ideas that cannot be inconvenienced are not scientific. They may be comforting. They are not progress.

title: On the Retention of Obsolete Theories
paras: Obsolete theories are not retained because they are true. They are retained because they are useful within a restricted domain, or because the cost of replacing them exceeds the cost of keeping them. Newtonian gravity is obsolete. It is also the reason spacecraft reach their destinations. The obsolescence is real. The usefulness is also real.

The retention is therefore not an error. It is a calculation. The calculation can be wrong. When it is wrong, the theory is eventually discarded. The discarding is rarely immediate. It occurs when a better calculation becomes available and when the institutions that teach the old calculation have been persuaded to teach the new one. The persuasion takes time. The time is measurable in textbooks.

title: A Remark on the Reader’s Patience
paras: The reader who has continued to this point has demonstrated a tolerance for sentences that contain both numbers and qualifications. The tolerance is not universal. It is also not permanent. It can be exhausted by repetition, by obscurity, or by the suspicion that the author is enjoying the sound of his own caveats.

The suspicion is sometimes justified. The caveats are nevertheless required. The universe does not become simpler because a clearer sentence would be more agreeable. It becomes clearer when the sentence matches the evidence. The matching is the only service the book can offer. The service is limited. It is still the service that was requested.

title: Worked Examples Throughout
paras: **Verbal** A ball thrown upward slows, stops, and falls. The same acceleration that slows it is the acceleration that speeds it on the way down. The direction of the acceleration never changes. Only the direction of the velocity changes.
**Calculation** A 2 kg mass falls 5 m. Potential energy lost = \( mgh = 2\times 9.8\times 5 = 98 \) J. If the energy appears as kinetic energy, \( v = \sqrt{2\times 98/2} = 9.9 \) m s\(^{-1}\).
**Verbal** Two slits produce a pattern of bright and dark bands. Closing one slit removes the bands. The bands require both paths. The requirement is not classical.
**Calculation** Light of wavelength 500 nm passes through slits 0.1 mm apart. On a screen 2 m away the fringe spacing is \( \lambda D/d = 5\times 10^{-7}\times 2 / 10^{-4} = 10 \) mm.

**Verbal** A star more massive than about eight solar masses ends as a neutron star or a black hole. The choice depends on the mass of the core that remains after mass loss. The dependence is observed in the remnant masses.

**Calculation** The Schwarzschild radius of the Sun is \( 2GM/c^2 \approx 3 \) km. A solar-mass black hole is therefore smaller than a city. A billion-solar-mass black hole has a radius of order \( 3\times 10^{9} \) km—roughly the size of the Solar System.
**Verbal** The cosmic microwave background is uniform to one part in \( 10^{5} \). The small non-uniformities are the seeds of galaxies. The seeds are visible. The galaxies are the grown plants.

**Calculation** A temperature fluctuation of 100 µK on a 2.7 K background is a fractional perturbation of \( 100\times 10^{-6}/2.7 \approx 3.7\times 10^{-5} \). The same fraction appears in the density perturbations that later collapse.
These examples use only the relations already stated in the relevant chapters. They recover the orders of magnitude that appear in nature.

title: About the Author
paras: Lothar J. Musiol is a graduate of Munich University of Applied Sciences who spent more than forty years in the semiconductor industry, first at Germany’s largest company in the field, then at a string of American start-ups. He studied physics alongside all of it, seriously enough to know exactly how much he is simplifying. Dual citizenship, put to its most sensible use, lets him split his time between San Clemente, California, and Passau, Bavaria, where Austria begins at the garden fence. The household includes one married daughter, one grumpy Teacup Pomeranian named Gucci, and eleven chickens, listed in order of seniority rather than volume.
He writes to make complex ideas clearer and more engaging than most treatments manage, without ever pretending they are simpler than they actually are.

title: The Philosophy of Science
paras: The philosophy of science examines the methods, foundations and implications of scientific knowledge. It asks what distinguishes science from non-science, how theories are confirmed or refuted, and what scientific claims mean.

Falsifiability, associated with Popper, holds that a theory is scientific only if it can in principle be contradicted by observation. Confirmation is never final. Refutation is decisive. The criterion is clear. It is not always easy to apply. Auxiliary hypotheses can protect a theory from apparent refutation. The Duhem–Quine thesis notes that theories are tested in bundles. A failed prediction can be blamed on an auxiliary assumption rather than on the core theory.

Kuhn described science as alternating between normal science, conducted within a paradigm, and revolutionary science, in which the paradigm is replaced. The description captures historical episodes. It does not supply a normative rule for when replacement is required. Lakatos offered research programmes with hard cores and protective belts. Progress is the prediction of novel facts. Degeneration is the accommodation of known facts by ad hoc adjustments.

Realism holds that successful theories are approximately true descriptions of an independent world. Anti-realism holds that success is empirical adequacy, not truth. Both positions are compatible with the same evidence. The choice is philosophical. The practice of science continues under either interpretation. The practice is the comparison of precise claims with observation. The comparison is public, repeatable and corrigible. Those features distinguish it from other forms of inquiry. They do not guarantee that the current claims are final.

title: Reichenbach on Probability, Time and Space
paras: Hans Reichenbach developed a frequency interpretation of probability, a causal theory of time, and a relational account of space-time. The frequency interpretation identifies probability with the limit of relative frequency in a long series of trials. The identification is operational. It avoids reference to single-case propensities. It requires that the series be infinite or that the limit be treated as an idealisation. Both requirements are explicit.

The causal theory of time defines the direction of time by the direction of causal processes and by the increase of entropy. The definition is not circular. Causal processes are those that can transmit marks. The mark method distinguishes causal from non-causal sequences. The thermodynamic arrow supplies the global direction. The two accounts are coordinated. Neither is reduced to the other.

The relational theory of space-time treats geometry as a system of relations among events rather than as a container. The treatment is consistent with general relativity. It emphasises that simultaneity is conventional within the limits set by the causal structure. The conventionality is limited. It is not arbitrary. The limits are those of the light-cone structure.

These positions appear, in different language, throughout the present book. The frequency interpretation underlies the statistical reading of the Born rule and of thermodynamic probability. The causal theory of time reappears in the discussion of the thermodynamic arrow and of the impossibility of signalling outside the light cone. The relational view of space-time is the background of the chapters on special and general relativity. The influence is not doctrinal. It is the shared insistence that claims about probability, time and geometry must be cashed out in terms of observable relations and operations.

title: Integration: Probability and the Born Rule
paras: The statistical reading of the Born rule is a frequency interpretation. The probability of an outcome is the relative frequency with which that outcome appears in a long series of identically prepared experiments. The identification is the one Reichenbach defended. It does not require a single-case propensity. It requires only that the series be long enough for the frequency to stabilise. The stabilisation is observed. The interpretation remains operational.

title: Integration: The Arrow of Time
paras: The thermodynamic arrow is the direction in which entropy increases. Reichenbach identified this direction with the direction of time and coordinated it with the direction of causal processes. A causal process is one that can transmit a mark. The mark method distinguishes sequences that can carry information from those that cannot. The coordination is retained in the present account. The increase of entropy supplies the global direction. The light-cone structure supplies the local causal constraint. Neither is reduced to the other.

title: Integration: Space-Time Relations
paras: The geometry of space-time is a system of relations among events. The relations are fixed by the causal structure. Simultaneity within a spacelike interval is conventional; the convention is limited by the requirement that no signal travel outside the light cone. The limited conventionality is the point Reichenbach emphasised. It reappears whenever coordinates are chosen in special or general relativity. The choice is free within the causal limits. It is not free outside them.

title: Further Integration: Common Cause
paras: Reichenbach’s principle of the common cause states that if two events are correlated and neither causes the other, then there exists a common cause in their past that screens off the correlation. The principle is a constraint on causal explanation. It is satisfied by the decay of a spin-singlet pair when the common cause is the preparation event. It is violated by the correlations of entangled particles when no local common cause is available. The violation is the content of Bell’s theorem. The principle remains the default assumption. Its failure is the signature of quantum non-locality.

title: Further Integration: The Direction of Time
paras: Reichenbach defined the direction of time by the direction in which entropy increases and by the direction in which marks can be transmitted. The two definitions coincide in the observed universe. They need not coincide in every conceivable universe. A universe that began in a high-entropy state would lack a thermodynamic arrow. Causal processes could still be defined. The observed coincidence is therefore a fact about initial conditions, not a logical necessity. The fact is the same fact that appears in the chapters on the low-entropy early universe.

title: Further Integration: Coordinative Definitions
paras: Reichenbach distinguished between axioms and coordinative definitions. Axioms are the formal relations. Coordinative definitions link the formal terms to physical operations. The distinction reappears whenever a theory is applied. The proper time of a clock, the length of a rod, and the simultaneity of distant events are fixed by coordinative definitions. The definitions are conventional within limits set by the causal structure. The limits are not conventional. The same distinction organises the relation between the mathematical formalism of relativity and the operations that measure its quantities.

title: Further Integration: The Relativity of Simultaneity
paras: Reichenbach showed that the simultaneity of distant events is fixed by a coordinative definition. The standard definition (Einstein synchronisation) sets the one-way speed of light equal in both directions. Other definitions are possible. They differ by a parameter \( \epsilon \) between 0 and 1. The choice of \( \epsilon \) does not affect observable round-trip times. It affects only the description of one-way processes. The freedom is limited by the causal structure. No choice permits a signal to travel outside the light cone. The limited freedom is the content of the relativity of simultaneity. It is conventional within the limits. It is not conventional outside them.

title: Further Integration: Probability and Induction
paras: Reichenbach treated induction as a procedure that converges to the correct relative frequency if a limit exists. The procedure does not guarantee success in any finite time. It guarantees that if a limit exists, continued application will find it. The guarantee is asymptotic. It is the strongest guarantee available for empirical generalisation. The same asymptotic character appears in the frequency interpretation of quantum probabilities and in the convergence of relative frequencies in statistical mechanics. The interpretation does not supply certainty. It supplies a method that succeeds if success is possible.

title: Further Integration: The Genidentity of Particles
paras: Reichenbach introduced the notion of genidentity—the identity of a thing through time. For classical particles the notion is unproblematic. For quantum particles it is not. Indistinguishable particles lack trajectories that can be followed. The absence is a consequence of the symmetrisation postulate. The postulate replaces genidentity with permutation symmetry. The replacement is required by the statistics. It is the reason identical particles are not individuals in the classical sense. The point reappears whenever the book discusses fermions, bosons or the failure of classical particle labels.

title: Evolution
paras: **Topics in this chapter** · Natural selection and differential reproductive success · The modern synthesis and later additions · Speciation and the biological species concept · Evidence from fossils, anatomy and molecular sequences

Evolution is the change in allele frequencies over time. Natural selection is the differential reproductive success of variants. The process produces adaptation. Given reproductive isolation it produces speciation. The theory is supported by multiple independent lines of evidence.

The modern synthesis combined Mendelian genetics with natural selection. Later additions include neutral theory, kin selection and the recognition of horizontal gene transfer. None replaces the core. The core accounts for the fit between organisms and environments and for the hierarchical pattern of similarity.

The fossil record, comparative anatomy, biogeography and molecular sequences all corroborate the same branching history. The history is not complete. The major outlines are robust. Open questions concern rates, mechanisms of speciation and the relative importance of selection and drift in particular cases.

title: The Standard Model of Particle Physics
paras: **Topics in this chapter** · Gauge group and particle content · The nineteen free parameters · Precision tests and the Higgs discovery · What the model does not explain

The Standard Model is a renormalisable quantum field theory based on \( SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \). It contains three generations of quarks and leptons and a single Higgs doublet. Nineteen parameters remain free. They are measured.

Precision tests confirm the model to high accuracy. The electron magnetic moment, the W and Z masses and the Higgs couplings agree with the predictions after radiative corrections. Neutrino masses require an extension. Dark matter and the baryon asymmetry lie outside the model.

The theory is the most successful description of the non-gravitational interactions. Its incompleteness is quantitative. No contradiction with existing data has been established. No complete ultraviolet completion is known.

title: Consciousness
paras: **Topics in this chapter** · The hard problem and the explanatory gap · Neural correlates and global workspace theories · Integrated information and higher-order theories · What remains unsolved

Consciousness is the presence of subjective experience. The hard problem is the question of why and how physical processes give rise to experience. Neural correlates identify brain activity associated with conscious states. They do not explain why the activity is accompanied by experience.

Global workspace theories propose that consciousness arises when information is broadcast widely in the brain. Integrated information theory quantifies consciousness by the amount of integrated information. Higher-order theories require a representation of one’s own mental state. Each theory accounts for some data. None is established.
The problem remains open. Progress has been made on the correlates and on the functional architecture. The explanatory gap between physical description and subjective experience has not been closed.

title: The Origin of Life
paras: Life is chemistry that persists, copies, and changes. How ordinary chemistry first managed that is unsolved.

The Earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago. Within a few hundred million years, perhaps sooner, the planet had water and a crust. By about 3.5 billion years ago, and possibly earlier, life was present. The evidence is chemical and structural: traces in ancient rocks that look like the work of microbes, and isotopes sorted in ways life sorts them. The dates are argued. The conclusion is not. Life started early, and it started small.

No one has watched it start. The laboratory can show pieces. In 1953 Stanley Miller and Harold Urey sparked a mixture of gases then thought to resemble the early atmosphere and produced amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. Later work showed that the early atmosphere was probably less helpful than they assumed, and that the blocks can form in other places: hydrothermal vents, drying ponds, impacts, the ices of space. Meteorites carry amino acids. The blocks are not the mystery. The organization is.

A living cell keeps a boundary, a metabolism, and a way to copy instructions. Which came first is the argument. Genes-first theories put copying at the center. RNA is the favorite molecule, because it can store information and catalyze reactions. An "RNA world" may have preceded DNA and proteins. Membrane-first theories put the compartment at the center. A bubble of lipid can grow and split, and chemistry inside can differ from chemistry outside. Metabolism-first theories put energy at the center. Vents on the seafloor offer natural proton gradients, the same kind of gradient cells still use. Each school has evidence. None has a cell.

The deeper requirement is a source of order that does not rely on a cell already being there. Energy flow can do that. A system that takes in energy and exports waste can maintain structure. Life, once started, is such a system. The origin problem is how the first structures became self-copying rather than merely persistent.

We should be honest about the gap. Origin-of-life research is a serious field with real constraints from geology, chemistry, and genetics. It does not have a standard model. When it does, the model will have to explain not only how the parts can form, but how they can assemble under conditions the early Earth actually offered, and why the genetic code has the form it has. Until then, the origin of life is the largest blank between cosmology and biology.

The geological constraints are tighter than the chemical possibilities. The early Earth was bombarded. It had oceans, at least intermittently, by about 4.4 billion years ago, judging from ancient mineral grains. It had land and water and mineral surfaces. It may have had an atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide and nitrogen, with less free oxygen than today. Oxygen came later, produced by life. Any origin scenario has to work under those conditions, or under conditions that local environments, such as vents or ponds, could have provided.

RNA is the leading candidate for an early genetic molecule because it can do two jobs. It can store a sequence, and it can fold into shapes that catalyze reactions. DNA stores sequence more stably and does not, by itself, catalyze. Proteins catalyze and do not, by themselves, store a replicable sequence in the same way. An RNA world, in which RNA did both jobs before DNA and proteins specialized, fits this division of labor. Laboratory RNA molecules have been evolved to copy other RNAs, though not yet to copy themselves with the reliability a living system would need. The gap is real and narrower than it was.

Membranes are the other early requirement that chemistry can supply. Fatty acids and related molecules form vesicles in water. The vesicles can grow by taking up more material and can divide. They can hold different chemistry inside than outside. A plausible origin does not need a modern cell membrane at the start. It needs some compartment that persists long enough for copying to matter. Mineral surfaces can also concentrate and organize molecules. They may have served as the first scaffolds.

Energy is the third requirement. A system that copies must be fed. Hydrothermal vents offer continuous chemical gradients. Alkaline vents, in particular, create natural proton gradients across mineral walls, and living cells still use proton gradients to make their energy currency. The resemblance may be a clue or a coincidence. Wet-dry cycles in ponds offer another energy regime, concentrating molecules and driving reactions that dilute water would not favor. Impact-delivered materials and atmospheric chemistry offer further inputs. More than one setting may have contributed. The origin need not have happened in a single kind of place.

What would count as a solution? A laboratory system that starts from plausible early-Earth materials, builds a compartment, a metabolism, and a copying molecule, and then evolves without further intelligent intervention, would be a powerful demonstration. No such system exists. Pieces exist. The distance from the pieces to the system is the current size of the problem. It is a scientific problem with constraints, not a mystery declared permanently closed to investigation. It is also not a solved problem wearing the costume of a solution.

The genetic code is part of the residue. Nearly all life uses the same mapping from DNA triplets to amino acids. The mapping is not random. Some features of it reduce the effect of errors. Whether the code was inevitable or a frozen accident is debated. Its near-universality is evidence that all known life shares an ancestry. It does not, by itself, say how the first copying began. Origin research and the last universal common ancestor are related subjects. They are not the same subject. The common ancestor was already a cell, with genes, a membrane, and a metabolism. The origin is whatever came before that cell.

One more constraint is phylogenetic. The last universal common ancestor was already complex. It had a membrane, a genetic code, ribosomes, and a metabolism. The origin has to reach that complexity, or reach something that could evolve into it. Scenarios that stop at a self-copying molecule have done something important and have not yet done the whole job. Scenarios that start with a metabolic cycle have the same gap in reverse. The full path is the unsolved problem. Partial paths are the progress. Both should be reported, and neither should be sold as the complete crossing.

Time is available. Several hundred million years separate the formation of a habitable surface from the first widely accepted evidence of life. That is a long interval for chemistry. It is a short interval compared with the history that followed. The early appearance of life is sometimes taken to mean that life starts easily. It may mean that. It may mean that we have only one sample, and the sample happened to start early. One sample cannot calibrate a rate. The early start is a constraint on scenarios, not a measurement of how common life is on other worlds.

Laboratory systems that evolve are the closest current approach to a demonstration. RNA molecules have been evolved to perform new reactions. Protocells have been made to grow and divide. Neither has been closed into a system that starts from simple feedstocks and runs without intervention. Closing the loop is the goal. Partial closures are the published progress. A reader should treat a headline that says life has been created in the laboratory as a claim to check against the actual system. The actual systems are impressive and incomplete. Incomplete is the accurate word. It is also a word that describes a field in motion rather than a field that is stuck.

title: Evolution and Genetics
paras: Once copying exists, evolution is difficult to avoid.

Copies are not perfect. Changes appear. Some changes make the copy more likely to be copied again, in that environment. Those changes become common. The process requires no foresight. It requires inheritance, variation, and unequal success. Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace stated the logic in 1858. The evidence since then has become overwhelming.

The evidence is fossil, geographic, anatomical, and molecular. Fossils sit in sequence. Transitional forms connect groups that once looked separate. Islands carry creatures related to the nearest mainland, modified. Bodies reuse structures: the bones of a hand, a wing, and a flipper correspond. Genomes reuse sequences. Humans and chimpanzees differ by a small fraction of DNA, and the pattern of difference matches a branching history, not a set of separate designs. Endogenous viral fragments sit in the same places in related species, scars of infections inherited from common ancestors.

Genetics supplied the mechanism Darwin lacked. Inheritance is carried by DNA, a double helix whose sequence of bases is read in threes. Each triplet specifies an amino acid, or a stop. Proteins, built from those amino acids, do most of the cell's work. A mutation is a change in the sequence. Most are neutral or harmful. A few are useful in some setting. Selection is the filter.

Evolution is not only selection. Drift, the luck of small populations, changes frequencies too. Genes move between lineages, especially in microbes. Development biases which variations appear. None of this repeals selection. It fills in the picture.

Evolution also does not mean "progress" in the moral sense. It means descent with modification. Bacteria are not failed animals. They are the most successful living things on Earth by number, by mass, and by tenure. Complex bodies are a late and local development. The history of life is mostly microbial.

The theory's power is that it connects. Antibiotic resistance, the fit of a moth to a tree, the useless hind limbs of a whale, and the shared code of all known life are one subject. A biology that rejected evolution would have to explain each of them again, separately, and worse.
